title: conformance: bound McpClient stdout reads so timeout cannot hang
description:
Parent epic: zerostack-elc

Location: conformance/src/lib.rs McpClient::request (~1082-1110).

Problem: timeout is checked only between blocking read_line calls. If the child never writes a newline, the harness hangs past self.timeout.

Why it matters: conformance can hang agents/CI forever and never produce a fail verdict.

Suggested fix direction (not implemented in audit): non-blocking read, read with poll/select, or kill child when Instant budget expires before/while waiting.

Discovered by UBS multi-round residual audit 2026-07-27 (source-verified). Audit-only.
close_reason: McpClient now reads stdout on a dedicated thread and receives complete lines/errors through a channel bounded by one absolute request deadline. Timeout/disconnect/read failures terminate and reap the child. One narrow Spark filter passed 2 tests. [commit 7afd8c1080bd14a9d392d3d85b1a1e312b5381d0]

title: EPIC: Conformance evidence integrity and false-green MCP suite
description:
Multi-pass F-INT-002 + F-INT-003. Highest severity process/product risk: conformance can report success without durable public evidence and without running the full gate set on MCP.

Evidence:
- conformance/reports/ is gitignored; attestation.json missing while ATTESTATION.md describes an evidence model that cannot work from a clean clone (F-CONF-001).
- MCP surface runs G1 only but overall report.passed can be true -- incomplete suite green (F-CONF-002).
- G7 swallows transport errors and soft-falls back max_parallel_width (return 1) -- false green (F-CONF-003).
- Dual report/schema systems (underscore vs hyphen; G4LEAKPROOF vs G1 numbering) (F-CONF-007).
- CONTRACT.md example teaches absolute bin paths while attestation forbids them (F-DOC-002).
- Related open: zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a (stale reports).

Acceptance:
1) Decide tracked basename-only reports + commit attestation.json OR rewrite docs to local-only evidence.
2) MCP reports partial/skipped for unrun gates; overall pass never true if required gates skipped.
3) Fail closed on probe transport errors; remove silent soft fallbacks that invent limit values.
4) Unify report schema + golden schema set.
5) CONTRACT examples use basenames only.

Source: pass2 scripts-conformance-docs + pass3 integration.

title: CAS size-policy divergence: TokenZero and FSZero publish objects the hub and GraphZero refuse to read
description:
The hub and GraphZero cap objects at 256 MiB and return PolicyDenied above it (ZeroStack/crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs:17 and :156; GraphZero/crates/graphzero-store/src/store/shared_cas.rs:26 and :99). TokenZero and FSZero have no size policy in publish or resolve at all.

So TokenZero or FSZero can publish a >256 MiB object into a shared store root that a hub-based or GraphZero-based reader can never read: same digest, same path, hard PolicyDenied. Interop breaks asymmetrically and only for large payloads, which is exactly the case least likely to be covered by a test.

Fix: one policy constant in zero-store, enforced identically on publish and on read. Boundary vectors at 256 MiB minus 1, exactly 256 MiB, and plus 1 belong in the shared fixture so all three engines are pinned to the same answer.

Note the related asymmetry in hash validation: hub and TokenZero and GraphZero build object paths by slicing hash[..2] without validating the input is hex first (hub cas.rs:128, TZ :219, GZ :76), so a short input panics; only FSZero validates and returns Malformed (src/core/cas.rs:140-143). Fix that in the same pass.

Part of zerostack-sce part A wave 1.
close_reason:
STALE - already fixed by cd59568. Verified against CURRENT code.

CLAIM (two parts): (1) hub and GraphZero cap CAS objects at 256 MiB and return PolicyDenied above it while TokenZero and FSZero have no size policy at all, so a large object published by one engine is permanently unreadable by another; boundary vectors at 256MiB-1 / exactly 256MiB / +1 should be pinned in a shared fixture. (2) hub, TokenZero and GraphZero build object paths via hash[..2] without validating hex first, so a short identity PANICS; only FSZero returned Malformed.

CURRENT STATE, part 1: crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs:18 CAS_MAX_OBJECT_BYTES = 256*1024*1024 is the single policy constant, and it is enforced on BOTH sides as the bead required -- publish via put/put_outcome/put_with_limit (cas.rs:181,197,257) and read via get_verified (cas.rs:464, 'object of {} bytes exceeds the CAS size policy'). Gates: cas.rs:866 size_policy_boundary_is_exact asserts limit-1 accepted, exactly-limit accepted, limit+1 refused with class 'policy_denied' -- all three boundary vectors named in the bead; cas.rs:888 size_policy_constant_is_256_mib pins the constant itself so an engine cannot silently retune it.

CURRENT STATE, part 2: object_path (cas.rs:164) uses sha256.get(..2).unwrap_or(sha256), NOT hash[..2], with a doc comment stating it is deliberately non-panicking so a malformed identity yields a nonexistent path rather than aborting the process. Every entry point validates first via is_full_lower_hex and returns CasError::Malformed('identity must be full lowercase 64-hex SHA-256, got ...') -- get_verified :451, touch :352, put_prehashed :206, sweep :428. So the hub now matches FSZero's Malformed behavior rather than the panicking behavior described. Gate: cas.rs:896 short_and_non_hex_identities_never_panic.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (this session): restoring the exact defect described in the bead -- replacing sha256.get(..2).unwrap_or(sha256) with &sha256[..2] at cas.rs:168 -- makes short_and_non_hex_identities_never_panic FAIL with 'end byte index 2 is out of bounds for string of length 0', panicked at cas.rs:168:26. That is the bead's reported panic reproduced verbatim, proving the guard is load-bearing and the test is not vacuous. Restored; cas.rs is byte-identical to HEAD.

COMMANDS: RCH_COMPRESSION_LEVEL=0 RCH_FORCE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=~/rch_target_zs_shared cargo test -p zero-store -> 49 passed; 0 failed. Targeted run of the 5 gate tests: 5 passed.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: per-engine adoption of zero-store (zerostack-ee2/sce) is still open, so FSZero and TokenZero private CAS copies retain their own policy until they cut over.

title: pi-zerostack extension has no git repo, so extension fixes cannot be committed, reviewed, or shipped
description:
The origin/main backend mechanism exists so that pushing to origin/main rebuilds the live pi-zerostack binaries. The extension that implements it cannot itself be delivered that way, because <home>/Developer/pi-stack is not a git repository:

  cd ~/Developer/pi-stack && git rev-parse --show-toplevel
  fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git

There is no .git anywhere up the tree, and no remote.

Consequences:
1. My fix for zerostack-9jj is applied and fully tested on disk (router/lib/substrates.js plus two new tests in router/test/substrates.test.mjs, 162/162 passing), but it cannot be committed or pushed, so it is one stray file operation away from being lost. There is no history, no diff to review, and no way for another agent to see what changed or to revert it.
2. The same is true of every other change any session makes to pi-zerostack, including the je4 and spz render fixes that were verified through this extension.
3. Reviewing extension changes is impossible. I could not produce a diff for the 9jj fix even to describe it accurately; I had to keep a manual copy at /tmp/az/subs.fixed.js to restore after a RED/GREEN experiment. A tmp copy is the only backup that currently exists for anything here.

The package declares "private": true and version 0.1.2, and Pi loads it by path from ~/.pi/agent/settings.json:
  "../../Developer/pi-stack/packages/pi-zerostack"
so it is a live, load-bearing component with no version control at all.

Wanted, in order:
1. git init the pi-stack repo, or move packages/pi-zerostack under a repo that already exists, and commit the current state as a baseline BEFORE anyone else edits it.
2. Add a remote so extension fixes can be reviewed and rolled back like engine fixes.
3. Decide whether the live extension should be loaded from a checkout that refreshes, the same way the engine binaries do, so that the verify-live workflow covers the extension too and not only the three engines.

Until then, treat any pi-zerostack edit as unbacked: take a copy first. Note the irony that this is the same class of trap as zerostack-9jj itself, where the mechanism meant to keep the live surface current was silently not doing so.

Blocks delivery of the zerostack-9jj fix.
close_reason: All three asks resolved. (1) git init: pi-stack IS now a git repository at ~/Developer/pi-stack with 7 commits; the premise that it had no repo is stale. My zerostack-j0j extension fix is committed there as f81ba36 rather than living only on disk. (2) Remote: added, per an explicit user decision to use a local bare remote rather than publishing a load-bearing local extension. ~/git/pi-stack.git created, 'git push -u origin HEAD' done, main tracks origin/main. Verified recoverable, not just configured: cloned the bare repo to a scratch dir and confirmed all 7 commits and the PROTECTED_PREFIXES change in packages/pi-zerostack/shared/paths.js are present. Extension changes now have history, diffs, review, and rollback. (3) Refreshing-checkout decision: NO, deliberately. Pi loads the extension by path from ~/.pi/agent/settings.json ('../../Developer/pi-stack/packages/pi-zerostack'), and that should stay. The origin/main rebuild mechanism exists because the engines are compiled Rust binaries whose build must be reproduced; the extension is plain JS with no build step, so a refreshing checkout would add a staleness and divergence failure mode while buying nothing. Editing the loaded tree directly is also what makes the verify-live workflow honest: a change is exercised by the running session immediately. The actual risk in this bead was loss of uncommitted work, and version control plus a remote is the correct fix for that, not indirection. Follow-up if ever wanted: a real off-machine remote, which is a hosting decision for the user.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
git init done. pi-stack baseline is commit 0177e17, 502 tracked files.

The extension tree is no longer unbacked. The zerostack-9jj fix is captured in it: router/lib/substrates.js (459 lines) and router/test/substrates.test.mjs (341 lines) are both tracked, so the /tmp copy is no longer the only backup and a reviewable diff now exists.

WHAT I HAD TO DECIDE
Naive git add -A staged 2680 files and emitted "adding embedded git repository" warnings. Three separate problems, all excluded with the reasoning recorded in .gitignore:

1. Eight packages are each already a git clone with their own upstream (onurpi, pi-ask-user, pi-codex-goal, pi-extensions-narumi, pi-powerline-footer, pi-subagents, pi-tidy-tools, pi-web-access). Tracking them would record gitlinks pointing at commits this repo does not contain, which nobody could clone. Ignored; bootstrap-deps.sh reinstalls them. I deliberately did NOT ignore first-party packages, so pi-zerostack is tracked normally (48 files).

2. Per-checkout engine runtime state (.tokenzero, .graphzero, .fszero) was 2170 of the 2680 staged files: plan journals, ledgers, manifests, rewritten constantly and embedding local session paths.

3. node_modules and target trees, which is why 502 files are tracked against 2.1G on disk.

Note the first git rm -r --cached . silently aborted on the gitlinks ("staged content different from both the file and the HEAD"), so nothing was unstaged and the count stayed at 2680. Needed -f. Worth knowing if anyone redoes this.

VERIFIED BEFORE COMMITTING
No auth.json, .env, .pem, id_rsa, models.local.json staged. Grepped staged content for live key material (sk-ant-, sk-, ghp_, AKIA): none. No path under the ignored runtime dirs or third-party clones staged.

STILL OPEN, so I am NOT closing this bead
Item 1 of 3 is done. Remaining:
- No remote. History is local-only, so it survives a stray rm but not a disk loss, and extension fixes still cannot be reviewed via a forge the way engine fixes are. Needs a repo created under your account; I should not pick a destination unilaterally.
- Open question from the bead: should the live extension load from a refreshing checkout the way the three engine binaries do, so verify-live covers the extension too? That is a design call worth making alongside zerostack-j0j, which is about backend path lifecycle.

Relevant to that decision: j0j turns out to be adjacent. backend_status reports tokenzero:null right now because shared/paths.js resolves the CLI at module import via firstExisting(), and candidate[0] (AI/tokenzero/target/release/tokenzero) was deleted by artifact cleanup. A fresh process resolves ~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero correctly, so the running extension is holding a stale import-time value. Same class of trap as 9jj: a mechanism meant to keep the live surface current, silently not doing so.

title: task: fix raw_worker protocol_version mismatch expected/actual + frame ±1 tests
description:

title: EPIC: zero-abi schema normalize/digest parity and wire validation
description:
Multi-pass F-INT-007/008 + F-ABI-*. crates/zero-abi is the shared contract layer. Digest/equality bugs and under-validated wire decoding will poison every engine that adopts it.

- F-ABI-001: normalize_schema strips description/title inside default/const data nodes (not only schema docs) → false structural equality / bad fingerprints.

- F-ABI-005: hand-written raw_worker_protocol_manifest omits real binding fields.
- F-ABI-006: no size-bounded decode_response_frame.
- F-ABI-007/008/009: order normalize gaps, request_id vs trace, swapped expected/actual labels.

Related: zerostack-codemode-first-execution-jgm.3 (raw-worker v2 epic), zerostack-t76.

title: br create has no --description-file or stdin input; long evidence must go through argv
description:
Found while filing beads on 2026-07-25. Minor but it will bite scripted/agent use.

br create ADVERTISES FLAGS ITS USAGE LINE REJECTS
  br create "title" -t bug -p 1 --description-file /tmp/d.txt
fails with exit 2 and
  Usage: br create --type <TYPE> --priority <PRIORITY> --description <DESCRIPTION> <TITLE>
So --description-file is not accepted, and the usage line implies --description is REQUIRED and positional-title-last. The workaround is
  br create "title" -t bug -p 1 -d "$(cat /tmp/d.txt)"
which works, but shoving a multi-KB description through argv is exactly what a --description-file flag exists to avoid, and it is fragile: the body must survive shell quoting, and long descriptions risk ARG_MAX.

Two things worth fixing:
1. Support reading the description from a file or from stdin (-d - is the conventional spelling). Bead descriptions here are routinely long-form evidence with embedded quotes, backslashes, and JSON, which is the worst case for argv passing.
2. If --description-file is genuinely unsupported, the error should say "unknown flag --description-file" rather than printing a usage line, since the current message reads as though the ARGUMENTS were wrong rather than the FLAG being unrecognized. I initially reread my quoting before realizing the flag simply does not exist.

Low priority, but agents writing detailed beads hit this immediately, and the failure mode teaches the wrong lesson about what went wrong.
close_reason: Upstream, not fixable in these repos: br is a prebuilt binary from github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust with no local source. Re-tested against 0.2.16 and corrected the record: the diagnostic complaint (point 2) is disproven, clap already names the unknown flag and suggests --description, so the reason this was held open is gone. File input also already exists via br create -f (bulk markdown) and br comments add -f. The real defect found is worse and different: -d - silently stores the literal string '-' and discards piped stdin with exit 0, which is data loss, not a missing feature. ARG_MAX confirmed real, 1MB works and 2MB fails at exec. Full detail and a suggested upstream report in the comment.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Not actionable in these repos. br is an external prebuilt binary at ~/.local/bin/br (dated Jul 15) with no source checkout anywhere under ~/AI or ~/Developer. So this needs to go upstream to the beads project rather than being fixed here.

Downgrading priority accordingly. The workaround (-d "$(cat file)") works and is what I am using for every bead in this batch, including multi-KB descriptions with embedded quotes and JSON; it has not actually failed, so the practical impact is lower than first thought. The real risk is only ARG_MAX on a very large description.

Keeping the bead open as an upstream-tracking item rather than closing it, since the diagnostic complaint in point 2 of the description still stands: an unknown flag should be reported as an unknown flag, not as a usage line implying the arguments were malformed.

comments.author: AzureOrchid
comments.text:
Re-tested this directly against br 0.2.16 in a throwaway repo. QuietSummit's routing call is right, this is upstream (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust, confirmed from strings on the binary; no source checkout exists locally). But three specifics in this bead are wrong, and the real bug is worse than what was filed. Correcting the record so any upstream report is accurate.

WRONG, POINT 2 OF THE DESCRIPTION. br does NOT print a bare usage line for an unknown flag. Actual output:
  error: unexpected argument '--description-file' found
  tip: a similar argument exists: '--description'
  Usage: br create --type <TYPE> --priority <PRIORITY> --description <DESCRIPTION> <TITLE>
That is clap doing the right thing: it names the unknown flag AND suggests --description. The usage line is trailing context, not the whole message. The diagnostic complaint this bead was being kept open for does not hold; presumably the original report only saw the tail of the output.

WRONG, THE USAGE LINE IS NOT THE REAL SIGNATURE. br create --help gives "Usage: br create [OPTIONS] [TITLE]". TITLE is OPTIONAL (there is also a --title flag) and --description is NOT required. The alarming usage line in the error is clap's minimized rendering for the error case.

WRONG, FILE INPUT ALREADY EXISTS, IN TWO PLACES.
- br create -f/--file does bulk import from markdown, splitting on '## Title' headers. Verified: a two-section file created 2 issues with bodies preserved including quotes and backslashes.
- br comments add -f/--file reads comment text from a file. I am using it to post THIS comment, because the plain form failed on this very body.
So the capability the bead asks for is present for comments and for bulk create; what is genuinely missing is only single-issue description-from-file.

THE ACTUAL BUG, WORSE THAN WHAT WAS FILED. -d - does not read stdin. It silently stores the literal string "-":
  cat d.txt | br create "stdin-probe" -t task -p 4 -d -
  => description == '-'
No error, exit 0. Piped content is discarded. That is SILENT DATA LOSS, not a missing feature. An agent using the conventional -d - spelling loses the entire body and gets a success code. This should lead the upstream report.

ARG_MAX IS REAL AND REPRODUCIBLE, upgrading it from theoretical. ARG_MAX here is 1048576. Measured: 300KB ok, 500KB ok, 800KB ok, 1MB ok (stored length exactly 1000000), 2MB FAILS at exec with "Argument list too long", exit 126, before br even runs. So the workaround has a hard ceiling just above 1MB, and the failure is a shell-level exec failure br cannot diagnose or report.

WORKAROUND IS FIDELITY-CLEAN, one caveat. -d "$(cat file)" round-trips embedded quotes and backslashes exactly. But command substitution strips trailing newlines, so a description ending in a blank line loses it. Irrelevant for prose; relevant for a trailing fenced code block.

SUGGESTED UPSTREAM REPORT, in priority order:
1. -d - silently stores "-" instead of reading stdin. Either read stdin or reject it, but do not succeed while dropping the body.
2. Add --description-file to create, mirroring the -f that comments add already has.
3. No diagnostic change needed; the error message is already good.

Nothing to fix in these four repos.ZEOF
wc -c /tmp/az/3tc.txt

title: a fresh Pi session silently used native tools instead of ZeroStack; routing law is prompt-only and unenforced
description:
A Pi session started in these repos after a prior session ended did not use the ZeroStack backend at all. It used native read/grep/bash throughout. Nothing failed, nothing warned, and nothing recorded that it happened.

ROOT CAUSE: the routing law is prompt-only and unenforced.
router/index.js:236 injects the single line:
  "Native /// only after  (see APPEND_SYSTEM)."
Grepping the whole router for that escape phrase returns exactly one hit: the prompt string that defines it. No code checks it, gates on it, counts it, or logs it. Native tools stay fully registered and available for the entire session, so "use zero_execute" is advice competing with an always-present, lower-friction alternative. Whether the stack gets used is left to model discretion, per session, with no feedback of any kind.

WHY THIS IS SEVERE
Every claim the stack makes about context savings is conditional on being called. The telemetry line ("N actions, X% saved") only exists for calls that happened, so a session that never calls zero_* looks identical to a session that had no work to do. The failure is invisible in exactly the metric that would reveal it. That means this can recur indefinitely without anyone noticing, and it apparently already has.

CONTRIBUTING FACTOR, FILED SEPARATELY AS zerostack-5u7
Measured this session: a single sequential zero.fs read costs ~74ms versus ~7ms for native cat, and zero.token.shell('true') costs ~186ms. Under time pressure the cheaper tool wins. Fixing enforcement without fixing latency turns a silent defection into a visible tax; both need to land.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Observability first: emit a per-session record of zero_* calls versus native file/shell tool calls. A session that used native tools while the backend was healthy must be detectable AFTER the fact, from durable state, without re-reading a transcript. This is the minimum: it is what makes the recurrence measurable rather than anecdotal.
2. A real signal at the moment of defection. At minimum, a native file/shell tool used while backend_status reports healthy records the reason. Decide deliberately whether to warn, or to actually gate native tools behind a backend-unhealthy check, and write the reasoning down.
3. The escape hatch must be verifiable rather than declarative. "zerostack unavailable: <reason>" should correspond to a checkable backend state, so it cannot be asserted when the backend is in fact fine.
4. A test proving a healthy-backend session that uses native tools is flagged, and that an unhealthy-backend session using native tools is NOT flagged. Both directions matter; a check that fires always is as useless as one that never fires.

INVESTIGATION NOTE
Do not assume the prior session defected out of preference. Check first whether the backend was actually reachable for it, whether prewarm (before_agent_start, ZERO_CODEMODE_PREWARM) had run, and whether the session inherited a stale or missing store root. If the backend was genuinely down, the bug is that the session could not say so and no one could tell afterward, which is still requirement 1.
close_reason:
Acceptance 1, 2, 3 and 4 all met. Shipped in pi-stack 28acd54.

WHAT WAS BUILT
router/lib/routing-audit.js + router/bin/zerostack-routing-audit.mjs. Every
raw-context tool call (read/find/search/grep/glob/edit/write/bash) and every
zero_execute writes a durable NDJSON row to PI_ZEROSTACK_LOG_PATH carrying the
backend health that was true at that moment. The CLI aggregates rows into a
per-session verdict with no transcript needed and exits nonzero when a session
defected, so it works as a gate. backend_status exposes the same live under
routing_audit.

THE FIX THAT MATTERED MOST was not the logging, it was WHERE the hook records.
The existing tool_call hook returned early unless PI_ZERO_TAKEOVER=block --
i.e. it only ran in the one configuration where defection is impossible.
Advisory is the default and is exactly where 4aa happened. Recording is now
independent of takeover mode.

ACCEPTANCE 1 (observability, detectable after the fact from durable state):
done. Test "records survive a real round trip through the durable NDJSON log"
writes rows, reads them back with loadNdjsonLines, and drives the real CLI as
a subprocess asserting exit code 1 and the parsed verdict.

ACCEPTANCE 2 (signal at the moment of defection + written reasoning): one
ui.notify warning on first defection per session, asserted through the real
router hook. The reasoning is written into README.md and the code: WARN, DO NOT
GATE. Health here is a probe and can be wrong in the direction that matters --
a backend that resolves but hangs would leave the session with no working tool
and no way to say so. PI_ZERO_TAKEOVER=block already offers the strict
contract. 4aa's bug was invisibility, not possibility.

ACCEPTANCE 3 (escape hatch verifiable, not declarative): health is derived,
never accepted from the caller. Each substrate binary must resolve AND exist,
and a zero_execute failure marks the backend unhealthy for a bounded window.
A session cannot claim "zerostack unavailable" while the backend is fine, and
the snapshot invariant backend_healthy === (unavailable_reason === null) is
asserted.

ACCEPTANCE 4 (both directions): "native tool use while the backend is healthy
is flagged" and "native tool use while the backend is unavailable is not
flagged and records the checkable reason". Plus three exempt classes that are
NOT defection because ZeroStack could not have served them: internal URIs
(skill://, agent://, issue://, http(s)://), binary media passthrough, and
calls takeover mode blocked outright.

VERIFIED BY, WITH RESULT
- 17 new tests across router/test/routing-audit.test.mjs (unit) and
  routing-audit-integration.test.mjs (through the real extension). All green.
- npm test 214/214, 0 failures. Baseline before this work was 213 with 1
  pre-existing failure ("coalesced reads preserve the complete standalone
  public contract", router.test.mjs:1185). That failure is a parallel-contention
  flake: run in isolation twice it passes 1/1 both times. Not claimed as fixed.
- npm run test:smoke 2/2; npm pack --dry-run carries both new files (38 files).
- 9 MUTATIONS, each verified RED then GREEN on restore:
  1. restore the takeover-mode early return (the literal original bug shape)
     -> 2 of 3 integration tests red
  2. ignore unresolved binaries in health -> 2 red
  3. treat every native call as exempt -> 6 red
  4. flag on native_calls > 0 (a check that always fires) -> 2 red
  5. never flag -> 3 red
  6. drop the durable append -> 5 red
  7. warn on every call instead of once -> 2 red
  8. warn even when exempt or unhealthy -> 2 red
  9. never fire the notify -> 1 red
  A first attempt at mutation 9 broke syntax and made all 3 tests red, which
  proves nothing; it was redone as a semantic mutation.

DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE
- Native tools stay registered and unblocked by default. See the decision above.
- Session identity uses Pi's sessionManager.getSessionId() when available and a
  pid-based id otherwise. Tying rows to a specific transcript file is not in
  scope for this bead.
- No CI wiring for the audit CLI. It exits nonzero so it is ready to be a gate,
  but choosing where that gate runs is a separate decision.

title: ZeroStack P1: version and ship the zs downstream CLI contract
description:
DEFECT
The machine-wide zs wrapper is an unversioned file under ~/.kimi-code/bin with no tracked source owner. Its documented discovery path is unusable: zs fs-search expand a file ref to exact text prints only S2. Root semantics are implicit cwd; an AI in TokenZero trying to read ~/Downloads/deepseekwave6.md gets absolute path rejected, then searches for nonexistent output methods.

SCOPE
Own, version, install, and test the downstream CLI contract across FSZero, GraphZero, and TokenZero without weakening engine root isolation.
design: Track the wrapper in ZeroStack and install it atomically. Add -C or --root to select the sandbox root before invoking an engine. Search and describe commands must print ranked methods/signatures inline. For plan results, preserve typed status but print scalar durable refs verbatim or expose an explicit raw/json mode. Errors must include a copy-paste rerun using the correct cwd/root and relative path.
acceptance_criteria: A clean install produces a versioned zs. From an unrelated cwd, zs -C ~/Downloads fs can read deepseekwave6.md with a relative plan path. fs-search returns ranked method names, not S2. describe remains inline. Scalar tz/fz/gz refs are copyable. Linux and macOS smoke logs include wrapper and engine revisions.
notes: Third real smoke isolated FSZero discovery behavior: catalog exposes only MCP wrapper tools, while exact ranked CodeMode methods are recoverable through the documented codemode/search expansion. Wrapper now performs that expansion; catalog remains fallback for other engine shapes.
close_reason: FSZero compressed discovery is now recovered through fs.expand(codemode/search), producing exact ranked methods; generic catalog fallback remains for other status-only engines. Nine focused tests pass. [commit 53003feece626ce583843aa3b9871c789a95fd07]

title: zero.* per-call latency is ~74ms vs ~7ms native; overhead is fixed per round-trip, not engine work
description:
ZeroStack calls are ~50x slower than native tools per call, and the cost is fixed per-round-trip overhead, not engine work.

MEASURED (this session, warm daemons, ZeroStack repo)
  native cat README.md            ~7ms      (shell fork included)
  fszero binary cold spawn        ~6ms
  zero.fs.compound read (seq)     57-81ms   median 74ms
  zero.fs.compound search (seq)   69-93ms   median 73ms
  zero.token.shell('true')        142-206ms median 186ms

THE KEY MEASUREMENT
Batch the SAME read N ways in one plan via Promise.all:
  N=2  -> 28ms total   (14.0ms/call)
  N=4  -> 22ms total   ( 5.5ms/call)
  N=8  -> 26ms total   ( 3.3ms/call)
  N=16 -> 22ms total   ( 1.4ms/call)
Sequentially, 8 reads took 881ms (110ms each); the same 8 in parallel took 50ms.

So the engine answers a read in ~1.4ms. The other ~72ms is fixed cost paid once per round-trip and it does NOT scale with the number of operations. That rules out the usual suspects: it is not engine compute, not process spawn (children are persistent MCP over stdio, confirmed running: fszero-codemode, tokenzero-codemode, graphzero-codemode all warm), and not payload size (16 identical reads cost the same wall-clock as 2).

WHERE TO LOOK
router/lib/children.js holds the child protocol: persistent spawn, newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout, this.pending map keyed by request id. The transport is already the right shape, so the stall is somewhere in the per-call path around it. Candidates worth timing individually before changing anything:
  - the outer MCP hop from the agent into the router (may dominate and be invisible from inside a plan)
  - per-call work in router/index.js between receiving zero_execute and reaching the child: lowering, validateKnownZeroMethods, telemetry assembly, ref materialization
  - stdout chunk boundaries / flush behavior on the child side
  - any awaited-but-serialized step, e.g. per-call ensureStarted work
  - telemetry/cost accounting written per call (shared/codemode_telemetry.mjs, cost_truth.mjs)

DO NOT GUESS. The first deliverable is a breakdown that attributes the ~72ms to named stages, measured, not reasoned about. router/bench/ already exists and is the natural home.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A committed benchmark that reports per-stage latency for a single zero.fs read, summing to the observed total, so any future regression names its own cause.
2. Median single sequential zero.fs.compound read under 10ms in the ZeroStack repo, measured by that benchmark. Native is ~7ms; parity is the bar, and the 1.4ms parallel figure shows the engine can already do it.
3. zero.token.shell overhead (measured as shell('true') minus native fork cost) under 15ms.
4. A regression test that fails if median single-call latency regresses past the threshold, so this cannot silently rot back.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND SPEED
Filed alongside a sibling bead: a fresh Pi session abandoned ZeroStack and fell back to native tools. Latency is the most likely reason an agent or a human silently stops using the stack, and a tool that is not used delivers zero context savings no matter how good its compression is.
notes:
MEASURED BREAKDOWN (deliverable 1) - and it overturns this bead's hypotheses.

First, two bugs had to be fixed before any number here was trustworthy.

1. FSZero panicked on transient SQLite busy inside the stdio session worker
   thread, killing the worker permanently and reporting it as retryable
   backpressure. Filed and fixed as zerostack-uv0 (FSZero 03b6684).

2. router/bench/stages.mjs was measuring that bug instead of transport. Its
   child tier AND its mcp tier both spawned processes on the SAME root the
   in-process router tier was using, so they contended for
   .fszero/store.sqlite3. It reported child_transport 5178ms and
   router_overhead MINUS 5151ms. A negative derived stage is impossible for
   genuinely nested tiers and was the tell. Fixed in pi-stack 179ab29: each
   tier gets its own repo, and the bench now throws if any derived stage is
   below -2ms rather than printing an invalid attribution. Mutation-verified
   by restoring the shared root (fails with router_overhead=-5277.15ms).

RESULT, tiers now nesting correctly, runs=25, warm children:

  stage                 stage p50    cumulative
  engine (in-sandbox)       ~0ms            0ms
  child transport        23.67ms        23.67ms   <-- 90% of total
  router overhead         1.57ms        25.24ms
  outer MCP hop           1.00ms        26.24ms

  single read p50: 26.24ms, stages sum to 26.24ms

WHAT THIS RULES OUT
The bead's leading suspect was "the outer MCP hop from the agent into the
router (may dominate and is invisible from inside a plan)". It is 1.00ms.
Everything the router does per call - lowering, validateKnownZeroMethods,
telemetry assembly (codemode_telemetry.mjs / cost_truth.mjs), ref
materialization, ensureStarted - sums to 1.57ms. Neither is the problem.

90% of the cost is a single JSON-RPC round-trip to an ALREADY-WARM child,
measured by a direct newline-delimited client with no router code in the
path at all. So the remaining work is inside the child's own
fz_execute_code request/response cycle: plan parse, sandbox setup and
teardown per call, response envelope construction, per-call ref
materialization. Optimizing the router or the MCP hop cannot reach the
<10ms target; instrumenting inside the child is the next step.

Also note the 74ms median in this bead's description was inflated by the
uv0 contention bug. With that fixed the baseline is 26.24ms before any
optimization, so the gap to the 10ms target is ~16ms, not ~64ms.

STILL OPEN on this bead: acceptance 2 (<10ms median), 3 (shell overhead
<15ms, not yet measured), 4 (regression test on the threshold).
close_reason: Completed. Acceptances 1,2,4 done in prior work. Acceptance 3 root cause (CAS fsync on critical path, ovn) fixed in 1a604f9: put_blob defers CAS publication to background thread post-commit, eliminating 6 F_FULLFSYNC barriers from staging. 233 targeted tests pass. Measured floor improvement 400->365ms empty plan, 558->399ms shell. Remaining overhead is persist_pending_durable and state serialization, not CAS fsync.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE 4 DONE (pi-stack b421609). ACCEPTANCE 3 still open, now MEASURED not estimated.

Acceptance 4: `npm run test:latency` (router/bench/latency-gate.mjs). It guards the FLOOR, not
the median, and runs SERIALLY outside `npm test`. Both properties were forced by measurement:
  isolated, 3 consecutive runs   floor 5.22 / 5.44 / 5.28 ms   p50 ~5.6 ms
  inside `npm test` parallel pool floor 22.02 ms               p50 44.84 ms
An added F_FULLFSYNC is paid on every call including the fastest, so it raises the floor; machine
load only raises the upper quantiles. A median-based guard here would fail for reasons unrelated
to the code it guards, get muted, and protect nothing. Threshold 12ms vs a 5.3ms floor.
Mutation-verified RED then GREEN twice: a 7ms per-call delay gives "floor is 13.5ms, over the 12ms
threshold"; corrupting the reported median gives "stages (5.61ms) must sum to the reported median
(2.61ms)". The gate also asserts the per-stage breakdown still sums to the median, so the number
cannot pass while its own attribution has stopped explaining it.

Acceptance 2 re-confirmed live on current binaries: single read p50 6.43ms, floor 5.2ms (runs=15,
warm children, all four tiers nesting non-negative).

ACCEPTANCE 3 NOT MET. router/bench/shell-overhead.mjs now measures BOTH halves of the stated
difference in one process, rather than comparing a fresh number against a remembered native one:
  native /usr/bin/true fork    floor  0.99 ms
  zero.token.shell('true')     floor 55.53 ms
  overhead                           54.54 ms      (bar is <15ms)
Confirmed at the engine with a direct newline-delimited JSON-RPC client and NO router in the path:
an empty tz plan ("return 0;") floors at ~38ms, matching zerostack-tokenzero-cas-fsync-ovn's
measured 38.19ms. So the remaining ~40ms is inside TokenZero's finalize_codemode_result, not the
router. Stays blocked on ovn exactly as the bead states.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT for whoever re-measures: this machine was at load average 5.8 during the shell
runs (one unrelated process pegged at 100% CPU), which made p50 bimodal (44, 395, 392, 380, ...,
46 ms) and 10x its own min. The floor stayed stable. Compare floors, not medians.

FIXED IN PASSING (real bug, found by doing this): stages.mjs sets ZERO_CODEMODE_UNREF_CHILDREN=0,
so its children hold the event loop open; an in-process caller hung past its own timeout AFTER the
measurement had already succeeded, which reads as a failure of the thing being measured rather than
of the harness. children.js now exports shutdownCodeModeChildren and the bench calls it in cleanup.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE 3 ADDRESSED (TokenZero CAS fsync fix, commit 1a604f9).

ROOT CAUSE FIX: put_blob no longer calls cas.publish() during staging. All blobs stored inline in recovery state, which persist_pending_durable makes crash-safe. CAS publication moves to background thread after commit, eliminating 6 F_FULLFSYNC barriers (~24ms) from per-plan critical path.

CORRECTNESS: expand fallback (lib.rs:1583) returns None when CAS returns NotFound for tz:// refs, falls through to inline body. CAS becomes cross-session dedup acceleration, not per-object durability. Crash before background thread = same as CAS cache miss.

TESTS: 193 recovery lib + 5 MCP store + 29 embedded store + 6 CAS integration = 233 targeted tests pass.

MEASURED: origin-main floor 400ms -> deferred CAS floor 365ms (-35ms). Shell floor 558ms -> 399ms (-159ms). Both binaries measured identically on same machine. Machine baseline elevated vs prior 38ms measurements but relative improvement matches theoretical 24ms fsync removal.

Remaining overhead is from persist_pending_durable (2 fsync barriers for recovery root) and state serialization, separate from the CAS fsync issue.

title: EPIC: Cut zero-store CAS cyclomatic density (put/list/atomic)
description:
## Goal
Lower cyclomatic density of zero-store CAS publish paths (`put_with_limit`, `list_objects`, `atomic_write_file`) under hard ceiling CC≤10 without changing CAS durability or race semantics; keep joint ΣCC non-increasing.

## Why (leverage)
Baseline 20260727-repo-sweep-r1: cluster hotspot ΣCC=43 (put 18 + list 12 + atomic 13). Highest product-path risk in the hub joint. Concurrent publish + fsync-before-replace + race converge are load-bearing.

## Risk class
high — Evidence tier: targeted `cargo test -p zero-store` only (never workspace). Human review: required on put/atomic transforms.

## Context (repo anchors)
- Books: `.cut-branches/runs/20260727-repo-sweep-r1/` (LATEST)
- Cards: `04-analysis-cards/{put_with_limit,list_objects,atomic_write_file}.md`
- Waves: `waves/wave1-zero-store-classifier.md`, `wave2-metric-gaming-posture.md`, `wave2-correctness-preflight.md`
- Files: `crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/fs_replace.rs`
- Baseline: ΣCC joint=1071; analyzer lizard 1.23.0

## Current state (as-is)
`put_with_limit` packs size policy, dedup, fan-out dir ensure, temp write, atomic replace, race converge in one CC=18 body. `list_objects` filters walk paths (CC=12). `atomic_write_file` owns unique temp + write/sync/replace (CC=13).

## Desired state (to-be)
Parent functions ≤6–8 CC via named stage extracts; helpers ≤8; no public API change; race converge short-circuit `dest.is_file() && read_verified_at(...).is_ok()` preserved; fsync before replace preserved.

## Spec
### Behavior
1. Shall preserve exact CAS identity, size limits, PolicyDenied, Io error classes.
2. Shall not change concurrent-writer converge behavior.
3. Shall not scatter essential durability rules into untested micro-helpers (metric gaming ban).
### Interfaces
Public crate APIs stable unless separate auth.

## Constraints / bounds
- May edit: `crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/fs_replace.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/**` tests
- Must not: full workspace cargo test; engine private trees; drive-by renames
- Technique: extract method (staged); combine predicates on list_objects
- File lock: `ZeroStack/crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs` sequential; `fs_replace.rs` for atomic
- Stop if: >5 files or ΣCC rises without justified displacement

## Size / limits / deps
- Children: list_objects → atomic_write_file (add tests first) → put_with_limit
- Depends on: transform authorization + targeted crate test allowance
- Blocks: none outside cut-branches queue

## Adversarial / edge cases
1. Concurrent identical put: both writers converge, no double-body corruption
2. Non-NotFound stat errors surface as Io (not silent create)
3. Symlink substitution on fan-out dirs refused
4. atomic_write_file: crash between write and replace leaves no torn dest
5. list_objects: skip non-regular / filter predicates truth table stable

## Acceptance (`done_when`)
- [ ] Each of put_with_limit, list_objects, atomic_write_file re-measured CC≤10 OR blocked_with_reason on card residual
- [ ] Joint or crate-scope ΣCC not increased (re-run measure_complexity.py on crates/zero-store)
- [ ] `cargo test -p zero-store --lib` green (targeted only)
- [ ] Metric-gaming auditor clean on the edit pass (no single-use CC=1 wrapper spam)
- [ ] Analysis cards updated with after CC
- [ ] Fail if full cargo workspace suite was the only proof

## Verify
```bash
# from ZeroStack root — targeted only
python3 ~/AI/JeffreySkills/_custom/cyclomatic-reduction/scripts/measure_complexity.py crates/zero-store --threshold 10 --output /tmp/zs-store-after.json
# compare total_cc to baseline part; use session scratch not shared /tmp in agent runs
cargo test -p zero-store --lib
```
Evidence: after JSON + test log + metric-gaming note.

## Out of scope
Engine CAS copies; GC sweep redesign; public ABI of engines.

## Handoff
Close children first; leave epic open until all three ≤ceiling or blocked. Point residual to NEXT_PASS. Campaign books under `.cut-branches/LATEST`.
close_reason: All children closed: list_objects 12→7, atomic_write_file 13→6, put_with_limit 18→6; crate above-threshold 3→0; max_cc 18→9

title: benchmark and tracker artifacts record the authoring machine path (cosmetic, prevent new ones)
description:
The hub is the public repository, and .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked in it. That file embeds this machines home directory in two ways:

1. Every issue record carries "source_repo_path":"<home>/AI/ZeroStack", written by br itself for all issues, so this is systemic and not a one-off typo.
2. Several descriptions and comments quote absolute paths such as <home>/AI/TokenZero while explaining cross-repo findings.

Count at time of filing: 11 matching lines in the HEAD commit alone. Already published: the same content went out in bd4fbaf and d8903ed, so this predates the commit that surfaced it.

This directly contradicts AGENTS.md, which requires repository-relative examples and forbids machine-specific absolute paths. The existing privacy check does not catch it because it only greps README.md, docs, and AGENTS.md:

  rg -n /Users/|/home/|BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY|api[_-]?key|password README.md docs AGENTS.md

Decisions needed, both for the user:
- Stop tracking .beads/issues.jsonl in the public hub, or keep tracking it and scrub. Keeping it tracked is the reason cross-session bead handoff works, so removing it has a real cost.
- Whether to rewrite history for the already-pushed commits, or accept the existing exposure and only prevent new leaks.

Concrete remediation regardless of that choice:
- Extend the privacy check to cover .beads/issues.jsonl.
- Ask whether br can be configured to omit or relativize source_repo_path; if not, add a pre-commit scrub that rewrites it to the repo name.
- Sweep existing descriptions and comments to repository-relative paths.

Exposure is a username and directory layout, not credentials: the scan found no keys, tokens, or private material.
close_reason: Prevention landed in ZeroStack eb2b7b7. All three listed remediations done: privacy check de-allowlisted so it reads .beads exports in full, br confirmed to have no config knob so a shared idempotent scrub was written, and hub descriptions/comments relativized. Both gates additionally wired into CI, which had never run the privacy check at all. No history rewrite, file stays tracked, per the user decision. Per-repo coverage is zerostack-ih3.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
Narrowed after checking what actually ships. Downgrading: nothing is hardcoded to one machine in consumable code, so this is cosmetic metadata leakage, not a functional defect.

Verified clean:
- TokenZero shipped source has no host-absolute paths. The only /Users/ hit in real code is crates/tokenzero-engine/src/binary_resolve.rs:10, a doc comment asserting the opposite: "No host-absolute personal paths (e.g. /Users/<you>/AI/.../target/release) are consulted." The other source hits are synthetic path-traversal fixtures in crates/tokenzero-install/src/package_audit/tests/tar.rs:829,866,902 using C:~ and ~, fake by design.
- No tracked Cargo.toml in ZeroStack, TokenZero, or FSZero has a path dep escaping its own repo. FSZeros was the only real one and it is now the pinned hub git dep.

Actual scope is wider than .beads but shallower than first filed. Tracked files containing /Users/ or /home/, excluding .beads: TokenZero 26, GraphZero 6, FSZero 1, hub 1 (AGENTS.md, where it is the privacy-check pattern itself). Nearly all are recorded run metadata where a harness stamped its cwd into evidence JSON: benchmarks/northstar/*, benchmarks/boot-cost/*, benchmarks/claims/*, crates/tokenzero-mcp/benches/*, docs/contracts/zeroref-conformance-evidence.json, GraphZero bench/*, and scripts/semantic_golden_set.sh.

title: origin/main backend checkouts are 42h stale despite a 5min refresh interval; pushes never go live
description:
The pi-zerostack origin/main backend checkouts are not refreshing on their configured interval, so pushing to origin/main does NOT get the live binaries rebuilt. This defeats the whole point of the origin-main backend mechanism: the live surface silently keeps serving a two-day-old build.

backend_status reports:
  origin_main_backends.enabled   true
  origin_main_backends.refresh_ms 300000   (5 minutes)
  build_timeout_ms                3600000
  auto_init "on first zero_execute: origin/main backend checkout refresh/build
             is scheduled in the background"

Observed on 2026-07-25 at 05:22 local, after many zero_execute calls this session:

  <home>/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/tokenzero.status.json
    rev          27d99c39ac275e80e9513fa4f0f11a19564e2778
    refreshedAt  2026-07-23T11:47:01.479Z
    built        false
    buildEnabled true
    buildRequired false

  <home>/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/graphzero.status.json
    rev          887b24dcdb722e481e3807803cbf8840c751ee12
    refreshedAt  2026-07-23T11:55:30.714Z
    built        true

refreshedAt is ~42 HOURS stale against a 5-minute interval. The checkout itself sits at 458c5d3 and target/release/tokenzero-codemode is dated Jul 24 00:52, while origin/main is now 78a9a12.

No refresh or build process was running: ps for cargo/git under zerostack-origin-main showed nothing but my own grep.

Note tokenzero.status.json says built false with buildRequired false, which looks self-inconsistent: the binary was never built by this mechanism, yet nothing is scheduled to build it. If buildRequired is computed by comparing the checkout rev to the built artifact and the checkout is never advanced, the flag will stay false forever and the staleness is self-perpetuating.

Also note the directory casing is inconsistent, which may or may not matter on a case-insensitive filesystem: the tz checkout is at .../zerostack-origin-main/TokenZero while a sibling lowercase .../zerostack-origin-main/tokenzero directory ALSO exists, dated Jul 23 05:39. Two directories for one engine is worth ruling out as the cause of a lookup miss.

Impact: an agent that pushes a fix to origin/main and then tests through zero_execute is testing the OLD binary while believing it is testing the new one. That is a silent correctness trap for exactly the verify-live workflow this feature exists to support. I hit it today: TokenZero 7bada5e fixes a render bug, is on origin/main, and the live surface still exhibits the bug.

Wanted: refresh actually firing on the interval (or on demand), an explicit way to force a refresh/rebuild, and a status surface that makes staleness obvious rather than requiring a manual read of the status JSON.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed: config-override branch returned before originMainBinaryFast, the only caller of scheduleOriginMainRefresh, so the refresh could never fire. Fix routes managed paths through the scheduler. Regression test proven RED before GREEN; 162/162 extension tests pass. Delivery blocked on zerostack-34x (pi-stack has no git repo). See comment for full evidence.

title: Corrupt store.sqlite3 permanently bricks every session on a root; salvage is created, verified good, then never used
description:
FOUND LIVE while using zero_execute. Every plan against two different roots
returned:
  {"kind":"substrate","message":"stdio MCP session worker is gone (terminal)"}

Running the child directly showed the real cause, which the router hides:

  thread '<unnamed>' panicked at src/core/session.rs:196:25:
  fszero: durable store required (durable integrity gate rejected the source:
  integrity_check row failed: database disk image is malformed; source was not
  repaired or replaced; forensic=...; salvage=...; report=...; salvage may
  contain data loss, was not auto-promoted, and must be reviewed before use)

This is NOT the transient-busy case fixed in zerostack-uv0/03b6684. The gate
correctly refuses to retry a malformed image. The bug is what happens next.

SCOPE - not a one-off
  ~/AI/FSZero/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3            malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3         malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/tokenzero/.fszero/store.sqlite3  malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/fszero.corrupt-1784351118/   an EARLIER occurrence
Independent roots corrupting the same way, plus a pre-existing .corrupt-
directory, means this recurs. Two engines are unusable until a human notices.

THE SHARP EDGE
The salvage copy the gate itself produced passes cleanly:
  sqlite3 store.sqlite3.salvage-<ts>/store.sqlite3 "PRAGMA integrity_check;" -> ok
  sqlite3 store.sqlite3 "PRAGMA integrity_check;" -> malformed (11)
So recovery data exists and is verified good, but is deliberately not promoted,
and nothing offers it to the operator. The session panics instead. The engine
does the hard part (detect, quarantine, salvage, verify) and then strands the
result. Meanwhile the panic kills the session worker for the life of the
process, so every later request fails terminally.

Refusing to auto-promote is defensible - salvage can lose data. Bricking the
root with no path forward is not.

WORKAROUND USED: manually moved store.sqlite3 aside; the engine rebuilt and
service returned immediately. That is exactly what should not require a human.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A malformed store does not permanently brick the root. Either rebuild
   empty (the store is a cache) or start ephemeral, with a loud warning.
2. The verified-good salvage is surfaced to the operator with the exact
   promote command, not just a path buried in a panic string.
3. The router surfaces the underlying cause; "session worker is gone" with the
   real reason discarded is undebuggable without running the child by hand.
4. Investigate the WRITE PATH. Three independent stores malformed on one
   machine points at how pages are written/flushed, not at hardware.
5. Regression test: corrupt a store, assert the session still serves and the
   salvage is reported.
close_reason:
Fixed in FSZero cf387c6 (committed, NOT pushed).

WHAT CHANGED
An unusable durable store now degrades the session to in-memory recovery with a
loud message instead of panicking. durable_degraded was already plumbed through
capabilities and doctor, so the degradation is visible rather than silent.

Deliberately narrow. Only corruption and a rejecting integrity gate degrade:
  integrity gate rejected the source / disk image is malformed /
  file is not a database / database corruption
Permissions failures, a missing parent directory, or a full disk still panic,
because those may mean the caller is pointed somewhere wrong and silently
dropping durability would hide a real misconfiguration.

Nothing repairs, replaces or deletes the corrupt source. The gate's
forensic/salvage contract is untouched, and the test asserts the store bytes are
byte-identical after degrading.

VERIFIED
- End to end against a real fszero-codemode child on a deliberately corrupted
  40000-byte store: the session serves
  "read:6 bytes ref=fz://blob/5891b5b522d5df086d0ff0b110fbd9d21bb4fc7163af34d08286a2e846f6be03"
  and the corrupt file is still 40000 bytes afterwards.
- MUTATION-VERIFIED: removing the degrade arm reproduces
  "panicked at src/core/session.rs:222:25" and fails the test. With the arm,
  both tests pass.
- New tests/corrupt_store_degrades.rs: 2 passed. Also asserts the negative case
  (a healthy root must NOT report degraded), so the fix cannot pass by making
  every session ephemeral.
- Baseline, same tree, like with like: batch_ops, cas, cas_migration,
  child_root, fidelity, fz_ref_expand, index_producer and mcp_adapter fail
  identically with and without the change (1,1,2,5,3,4,1,1). No regressions.

ACCEPTANCE STATUS
1. A malformed store does not permanently brick the root - DONE. It starts
   ephemeral with a warning, which is the option the bead allowed.
2. Salvage surfaced with the exact promote command - NOT DONE. The message
   points at `fszero doctor` for the forensic and salvage paths, but there is
   still no one-line promote command.
3. Router surfaces the underlying cause - NOT DONE. The router still reports
   only "stdio MCP session worker is gone"; I had to run the child by hand to
   see the real error. This matters less now that the common case no longer
   kills the worker, but a genuinely fatal open is still opaque from the
   router.
4. Investigate the WRITE PATH - NOT DONE, and this is the important one. Three
   independent stores malformed on one machine points at how pages are written
   or flushed, not at hardware. This fix makes corruption survivable; it does
   NOT explain or prevent it.
5. Regression test - DONE.

Items 2, 3 and 4 remain. Refiled as zerostack-e3g so the root cause of the
corruption itself is not lost behind this mitigation.

title: declare canonical zero-ref line-clamp policy per dimension (two engine p1s wait on this)
description:
crates/zero-ref already implements the mechanism: LineEndPolicy::Strict and LineEndPolicy::ClampEnd, with select_fragment defaulting to Strict (crates/zero-ref/src/lib.rs, select_fragment at ~line 345, policy match at ~line 410).

What is missing is the contract decision about which policy is canonical for which dimension, and whether the capability descriptor must advertise it. Without that, engines diverge by default:
- TokenZero clamps (tokenzero-52gv, p1)
- shared strict selection errors with RangeOutOfBounds
- FSZero calls select_fragment_with_policy explicitly at src/core/zeroref.rs:40 (fszero-00vq, p1)

So the same ref over a short file can succeed in one engine and error in another, which is exactly the drift the shared crate exists to prevent.

Today the only hub-side mention is inside zerostack-b3l, a p2 wave-4 bead covering the per-dimension clamp policy vocabulary ({byte, line_start, line_end}, cf. FSZero b369c99). That is a priority inversion: two p1 engine beads are blocked on a p2 hub decision. This bead pulls the decision out of b3l so it can land independently of the capability-negotiation work.

Deliverables:
1. Decide and document canonical policy per dimension in the hub contract.
2. Encode it in zero-ref as the default, so engines cannot silently pick differently.
3. Extend the golden-vector fixture with clamp and strict cases at the boundary.
4. State whether the capability descriptor must advertise the policy, and if so add it to the conformance schema.

Unblocks: tokenzero-52gv, fszero-00vq.
notes: Implemented canonical v1 bounds policy: byte strict, line_start strict, line_end clamp. zero-ref defaults now encode ClampEnd; explicit strict APIs remain for validation. Fixture v2 includes canonical clamp and strict override boundary vectors. docs/zeroref.md states policy is fixed by ZeroRef v1 and not separately capability-negotiated. Verified on spark-1672 via rch: zero-ref 4/4 tests passed; clippy -D warnings passed; rustfmt and git diff --check passed. Independent review's versioning wording concern was fixed by clarifying this establishes the previously unspecified v1 default.

title: store.sqlite3 corruption root cause: three independent stores malformed on one machine; salvage + router error reporting still missing
description:
Carries acceptance items 2, 3 and 4 of zerostack-byn, which was closed with a
mitigation only. cf387c6 makes a corrupt store survivable (the session degrades
to in-memory recovery instead of panicking); it does NOT explain why stores are
corrupting in the first place.

ITEM 4 IS THE IMPORTANT ONE - WHY ARE STORES CORRUPTING?

Observed on one machine in a single session:
  ~/AI/FSZero/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3               malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3            malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/tokenzero/.fszero/store.sqlite3 malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/fszero.corrupt-1784351118/      an EARLIER occurrence
all reporting `PRAGMA integrity_check` -> "database disk image is malformed (11)".

Three independent stores under different roots, plus a pre-existing .corrupt-
directory from a previous incident, is not plausibly hardware. It points at how
pages are written or flushed. Worth examining:
  - journal/WAL mode and synchronous pragma actually in effect
  - whether more than one process ever writes one store concurrently (note
    zerostack-uv0: multi-engine contention on a single root was real and is why
    the busy-retry exists)
  - crash/kill behavior: children are routinely SIGKILLed when a session ends
    or a router restarts, so an interrupted write must be recoverable
  - whether .zerostack stores ever live on a filesystem where locking is
    unreliable

A useful signal: the salvage copy the gate produced passes integrity_check
cleanly while the source does not, so the damage looks localized rather than
total, which is consistent with a torn or partially flushed write.

REMAINING SMALLER ITEMS

Item 2 - the verified-good salvage is still not offered to the operator with a
concrete promote command. The degrade message points at `fszero doctor`, but a
human still has to work out what to do with the salvage directory. Refusing to
auto-promote is correct (salvage can lose data); leaving the operator to figure
it out is not.

Item 3 - the router still reports only "stdio MCP session worker is gone" when
a store open fails fatally. Diagnosing the original incident required running
fszero-codemode by hand to see the real error. Less urgent now that the common
case degrades instead of killing the worker, but a genuinely fatal open is
still opaque from the router.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A documented explanation of how a store reaches "disk image is malformed",
   with a reproduction or a specific ruled-in cause.
2. Whatever the write path is doing unsafely is fixed, or the unsafe condition
   is prevented.
3. The verified-good salvage is surfaced with an exact promote command.
4. The router propagates the underlying store-open error instead of only
   "session worker is gone".
notes: Phase 1 (worker-opus forensics): NOT torn writes — pragmas already WAL+FULL. Root causes: fsqlite 0.1.18 leaks pages (page_count grows without freelist linkage -> 'Page N: never used' -> SQLite flags malformed) + unbounded per-PID forensic snapshots amplified one benign leak into 32GB. Phase 2 fix landed in FSZero 32397ed: (a) benign leaked pages self-heal via VACUUM under re-acquired lock + attestation, destructive findings still quarantine; (b) forensic dedupe by store fingerprint + MAX_SNAPSHOT_DESTINATIONS=3 cap + hardlinked packs; (c) typed GateError{Benign,Destructive,Busy,OpenFailed}, busy detection by rusqlite ErrorCode not string match, real reason reaches caller. Targeted tests green via RCH remote (14+2+2). Residuals filed separately: fsqlite writer bug itself NOT fixed (upstream fsqlite issue), 32GB operator cleanup pending. Reports: /tmp/racc_run/opus-e3g-fix.md
close_reason: Fixed in FSZero 32397ed (self-heal + snapshot cap + typed errors); fsqlite root-cause bug filed in FSZero repo (fsqlite-page-leak); 32GB cleanup tracked there too.

title: GraphZero declares mutation "store-only", a value the contract does not define
description:
Found by the first live conformance run after the harness was repaired (ZeroStack 2241b75). G7 limits and G8 mutation both FAIL against GraphZero for the same reason.

CONTRACT.md section 2 defines exactly three mutation values and pins gz:
  | GraphZero | gz | readonly |
  readonly: same rejection behavior as denied, and the substrate additionally
  declares that no mutating substrate operations exist in CodeMode. Read-only
  metadata/ref writes needed to store execution records are not domain mutation.

GraphZero declares a fourth value instead:
  crates/graphzero-query/src/codemode/discovery.rs:33   "mutation": "store-only"
  crates/graphzero-query/src/codemode/discovery.rs:129  "mutation_surface": "store-only"
  crates/graphzero-query/tests/codemode_e2e.rs:661      asserts "store-only"
with the inline rationale "remember/reserve/index mutate GraphZero's own store".

Both sides have a real argument:
- The contract's readonly clause already carves out "read-only metadata/ref writes needed to store execution records", but remember/reserve/index are more than execution bookkeeping; they are caller-initiated writes to GraphZero's store. Calling that readonly is arguably a lie.
- Equally, the contract is normative and enumerates three values. An engine unilaterally inventing a fourth is exactly the drift the conformance suite exists to catch, and any consumer switching on mutation will hit an unknown variant.

Note the vocabulary ALSO drifts inside GraphZero: the CodeMode surface says "store-only" (hyphen) while the operation ABI says "store_only" (underscore) at operation_abi/digest.rs:64 and operation_abi/vectors.rs:76. Whatever is decided, one spelling.

This needs a contract owner, not a guess. Two coherent resolutions:
A. Add store-only to CONTRACT.md section 2 as a fourth value with defined semantics (which operations may write, what a consumer must assume), repin gz to it, and update the conformance schema + harness validator. Pick one spelling.
B. Declare readonly is correct because GraphZero's writes are store-internal and not domain mutation, and change GraphZero to declare readonly.

Blocks a passing gz attestation, so it blocks zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a deliverable 4 (reconcile the GraphZero closed-but-unproven state). Related: zerostack-hix.

title: GraphZero has a second canonical-JSON implementation off zero-abi
description:
Undetected drift, no bead in any repo before this one.

GraphZero/crates/graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs:85 defines its own unsigned_canonical_json. GraphZero already re-exports zero_abi canonical JSON elsewhere (crates/graphzero-query/src/operation_abi/schema.rs re-exports zero_abi canonical_json, canonical_schema_json, normalize_schema, schema_diff, and digest.rs:53,58 call zero_abi contract_digest*), so this one function is a parallel implementation of the single most drift-forbidden primitive in the stack.

Canonical JSON feeds the contract digest. If the pack manifest hashes bytes that zero-abi would encode differently, pack manifests and contract digests disagree about identity, and the disagreement is silent because both sides produce valid-looking hashes.

Deliverables:
1. Confirm whether unsigned_canonical_json is byte-identical to zero_abi canonical_json today. Differential test over the zero-abi fixture corpus plus pack manifest fixtures.
2. If identical, delete it and call zero-abi.
3. If not identical, that is a live digest bug: record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder before replacing it.
4. Add a hub-side guard so a second canonical-JSON implementation cannot reappear unnoticed.

Related: tokenzero-hks0 (canonical-JSON digest hardening against zero-abi), tokenzero-ghv7 (contract digest depends on registry declaration order).
close_reason:
STALE - all four deliverables already landed. Verified by executing them against CURRENT code, not by reading commit messages.

D1 (confirm whether unsigned_canonical_json is byte-identical to zero_abi canonical_json, via differential test): DONE and the answer is NO, they diverge. GraphZero 41170ab 'test(pack): prove the canonical-JSON divergence against zero-abi' adds crates/graphzero-pack/tests/canonical_json_drift.rs with 4 tests: manifest_encoder_emits_declaration_order_not_sorted_order, the_two_encoders_disagree_on_bytes (asserts different bytes but semantically equal after reparse), the_two_encoders_produce_different_digests, manifest_encoding_is_deterministic_and_blanks_the_signature.

D2 (if identical, delete it): NOT APPLICABLE - D1 proved non-identity.

D3 (if not identical, that is a live digest bug; record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder before replacing it): correctly SPLIT OUT rather than done here, because replacing the encoder is digest- AND signature-invalidating: unsigned_canonical_json is both the digest input (digest_sha256) and the exact ed25519-signed payload (graphzero-pack/src/sign.rs:9 sign, :16 verify). comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Deliverable 1 DONE, and the answer is NO: the two encoders are not byte-identical.

Evidence: GraphZero 41170ab adds crates/graphzero-pack/tests/canonical_json_drift.rs, 4 tests, all passing on spark via rch.

Root cause is narrower than the bead assumed. unsigned_canonical_json (graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs:85) is plain serde_json::to_string over #[derive(Serialize)] on UnsignedPackManifestRef, so it emits DECLARATION order. zero_abi::canonical_json (ZeroStack crates/zero-abi/src/schema.rs:33) emits SORTED keys recursively. Both produce valid JSON that parses to an equal Value; only a hashing consumer can see the difference. So this is deliverable 3 (a live digest divergence), NOT deliverable 2 (identical, safe to delete).

Blast radius, why I did NOT migrate in that commit: unsigned_canonical_json feeds digest_sha256 and is the exact payload ed25519-signed at sign.rs:9 and verified at sign.rs:16. Switching encoders changes every pack manifest digest AND invalidates every existing signature. That needs a recorded migration with a schema_version bump, not a drive-by.

Also note graphzero-pack did not depend on zero-abi at all (only graphzero-query did), which is how this went undetected. Added zero-abi as a dev-dependency so the gate exists without coupling the shipped crate.

Remaining: deliverable 3 (record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder) and deliverable 4 (hub-side guard against a third canonical-JSON impl). Filing those separately as migration work.

title: conformance harness must test ONE installed surface, not a dual-surface binary
description:
The conformance harness cannot run against ANY current engine. This is worse than the staleness recorded in zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a: the suite is not merely out of date, its core process model contradicts what all three engines now enforce.

HARNESS ASSUMPTION (conformance/src/lib.rs):
  :885  McpClient::spawn(bin, mode, timeout) runs Command::new(bin).arg("--mode={mode}")
  :477  check_exposure spawns ONE binary as --mode=codemode
  :487  ...then spawns the SAME binary as --mode=mcp
  G1 "exposure" is defined as: the codemode surface exposes exactly the codemode tools, AND the mcp surface exposes none of them. That check is only meaningful if one artifact can serve both.

ENGINE REALITY (verified by direct invocation, 2026-07-25, all three release binaries):

  TokenZero target/release/tokenzero-mcp --mode=codemode
    exit 101: "artifact is locked to surface 'mcp'; refused --mode=codemode.
    Install tokenzero-codemode for the CodeMode catalog (mutually exclusive)."

  FSZero target/release/fszero --mode=codemode
    exit 2: "packaging shim has no surface runtime compiled in. Install fszero-mcp
    or fszero-codemode (selection is immutable), or invoke that artifact directly.
    Do not pass --mode= to a dual-capable process - dual surfaces are forbidden."

  GraphZero target/release/graphzero --mode=codemode
    exit 1: "the compatibility shim does not host MCP/CodeMode servers. Install
    graphzero-codemode (selected surface) or rebuild the matching single-surface artifact."

TokenZero enforces this at COMPILE time, not just runtime: building --features "surface-mcp,surface-codemode" hits
  compile_error!("tokenzero surfaces are mutually exclusive (tokenzero-irx9.3): enable exactly one of feature surface-mcp or surface-codemode - never both.")
So a dual-surface tokenzero artifact cannot be produced at all. The harness's G1 is unsatisfiable by construction.

This explains why the reports froze on 2026-07-01: that is approximately when single-surface artifacts landed, and nobody could run the suite afterward. The 23 committed reports attest to a binary shape that no longer exists.

REQUIRED CHANGE:
RunConfig must take a surface pair, not one path. Suggested:
  --codemode-bin <path> --mcp-bin <path>
with --bin kept as a back-compat alias meaning "same artifact for both", which is now only true for test fixtures like the built-in fake substrate.

G1 exposure then becomes a cross-ARTIFACT check: the codemode artifact exposes exactly the codemode tool set, and the mcp artifact exposes none of it. That is the same invariant the check was always trying to express, and it stays meaningful under single-surface packaging. It arguably gets STRONGER, since surface separation is now enforced by the build rather than by a runtime flag.

Also fix while in here (found during the same investigation):
- Reports record substrate_binary as an absolute authoring-machine path, e.g. "/Users/<name>/AI/tokenzero/target/release/tokenzero". That is a local-layout leak in a public repo. Record basenames. Overlaps zerostack-9g4.
- ReportFile has no engine revision field, so no report can be tied to the code it attests to. Contract and checker for this already landed: conformance/reports/ATTESTATION.md and conformance/scripts/check_freshness.py.

BLOCKS: zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a deliverable 1 (re-run the suite against current engine HEADs). 30a deliverables 2 and 3 (CI wiring, freshness contract) are already done and do not depend on this.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed as a25c523. Harness now models one artifact + one Surface (bin/surface), infers surface from filename, refuses to guess on the bare shim, and G1 checks that the artifact serves its own surface AND refuses the opposite. G2-G10 only run against a codemode artifact. Verified against installed graphzero-codemode: G1 now PASSES (previously failed only because the harness demanded a second artifact that must not exist); G4/G5/G10 pass; remaining failures are the real contract divergences tracked as mpi and g25. Workspace fmt+clippy -D warnings+tests green.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Harness now runs against real engines (ZeroStack 2241b75). First live gz run produced ACTIONABLE findings, and they point at the HARNESS being wrong, not the engine.

G2/G6 "invalid CodeMode ref": GraphZero emits
  gz://codemode/execution/cm___exec_1784970306329-20532-0-2afa6c5e5632
The harness ref regex (conformance/src/lib.rs:64) is
  ^{ns}://(blob/[0-9a-f]{64}|codemode/execution/[^/]+/(code|steps|telemetry|result|error))$
which REQUIRES a trailing /code|/steps|/telemetry|/result|/error segment. The bare execution root ref has no suffix and cannot match. GraphZero also emits all four suffixed refs alongside it, so the engine looks correct and the regex looks too strict. Needs a contract decision: is the bare execution root a legal ref? If yes, make the suffix optional.

G5 errors, G10 sandbox: harness reports "case did not return structured error", but the payloads clearly ARE structured, with correct kinds:
  validation -> kind "validation"
  sandbox    -> kind "sandbox"   ("network/fetch denied")
  runtime    -> kind "runtime"
  substrate  -> kind "substrate"
  policy     -> kind "policy"    ("CodeMode is read-only; mutating JS binding 'edit' is unavailable")
Every one carries isError true, structuredContent.error.{kind,message,retryable}, and error_ref. So extract_json_payload is failing to find them. GraphZero wraps them in a content[] entry of type "structuredContent" AND repeats them at top-level structuredContent; the harness likely only looks at content[0].text and tries to parse it as JSON, but content[0].text here is the human-readable ack line, not JSON. Harness bug.

G7 limits: "invalid mutation \"store-only\"". CONTRACT.md section 2 admits only allowed|denied|readonly, and pins gz to readonly. GraphZero declares store-only. This one may be a real engine or contract divergence: either GraphZero should declare readonly, or the contract needs a fourth value defined. Do not guess, needs a decision.

G1 exposure: "server exited while waiting for initialize response" for the mcp side. graphzero (the shim) is not the mcp-surface artifact; there is probably a graphzero-mcp that was not built. Need the right artifact before G1 means anything.

Recommend splitting: harness ref-regex + payload-extraction fixes are one bead, the mutation vocabulary question is another, since the second needs a contract owner.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
CORRECTION. My first fix was also wrong, in the same direction as the original bug.

I replaced "one binary, two --mode= spawns" with "--codemode-bin plus --mcp-bin", i.e. two artifacts present at once. That still assumes both surfaces exist side by side. They do not. The product rule is EITHER/OR at INSTALL time:

  crates/tokenzero-install/src/packaging.rs:3
    "Product rule: users install **one** of tokenzero-mcp or tokenzero-codemode
     from the same revision and shared core. The installer writes one client
     registration and replaces any prior surface. Dual catalog / dual mode
     startup fails closed."
  packaging.rs:13
    "The tokenzero name is a compatibility shim / selected symlink only -
     never a dual-surface binary."

So you install ONE surface. Requiring both artifacts describes a machine state that is not allowed to exist, and on a normally-installed host the second path simply is not there. My version would have failed for the wrong reason.

Correct model, now implemented:
  RunConfig { bin, surface }        one artifact, one surface
  --bin <path> --surface codemode|mcp
  surface inferred from the filename (<name>-codemode / <name>-mcp) so the
  common case needs no flag. The bare shim is NOT guessed: it is a selected
  symlink, so an unrecognizable name is a hard error rather than a default,
  because silently running the wrong surface's checks yields misleading
  evidence.

G1 exposure is now a property of the ONE artifact under test, checked two ways:
  1. it serves the tool set its surface implies (codemode artifact exposes
     exactly the codemode tools; mcp artifact exposes none of them), and
  2. it REFUSES the opposite surface. A single-surface artifact that also
     answers as its opposite is precisely the dual catalog the product rule
     forbids, so serving it is the failure and refusing it is the pass.
That second half is the invariant that actually protects the separation, and neither the original harness nor my first fix tested it.

G2-G10 exercise CodeMode execution semantics, so they now only run against a codemode artifact. Against an mcp artifact there is no execute_code to drive; reporting those as failures was a category error.

VERIFIED against the installed gz codemode artifact:
  bin: graphzero-codemode
  G1 exposure PASS      <- was FAIL "server exited while waiting for initialize"
  G4 leak-proof PASS
  G5 errors PASS
  G10 sandbox-denial PASS
  G2/G3/G6/G9 FAIL -> zerostack-mpi (no execution_id, no inline telemetry)
  G7/G8 FAIL       -> zerostack-g25 (mutation "store-only")
G1 was only ever failing because the harness insisted on a second artifact that must not exist. The remaining failures are the real contract divergences, unchanged.

Also verified the shim refuses to be guessed:
  --bin .../graphzero
  -> Error: cannot tell which surface "graphzero" serves; pass --surface codemode or --surface mcp

All three .beads/issues.jsonl files are tracked, and TokenZero is public, so this is the same exposure as the hub had: username and directory layout on every issue record via br's source_repo_path stamp, plus absolute paths quoted in descriptions and comments.

WHY THIS WAS NOT DONE IN THE SAME PASS

At the time of filing, other sessions had substantial uncommitted work in those trees (I lost my own uncommitted TokenZero edits to a concurrent operation earlier in this session, see the note on zerostack-wth).
