DELIVERABLES
1. Run the scrub in TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero, one commit per repo, when the tree is quiet and the other sessions have committed.
2. Verify integrity the same way the hub was verified, and do not skip this: record count unchanged, id order unchanged, per-record key sets unchanged, and only source_repo_path, description, and comments differing. The hub check caught nothing wrong, but a silent field loss across 846 records would be very hard to notice later.
3. Copy or reference the two gates into each engine repo's CI, since a scrub with no gate will simply rot the moment the next br sync runs. The hub runs both check_no_host_paths.py and scrub_beads_export.py --check in a privacy job.
4. Add the scrub to each repo's documented br sync recipe, as was done in the hub AGENTS.md, so it is a required step rather than folklore.

Note the ordering constraint: the scrub must run AFTER br sync --flush-only and BEFORE git add, because br rewrites the export from SQLite on every sync and will reintroduce the absolute path each time. A one-time scrub without the recipe change and the CI gate accomplishes nothing durable.

Decide whether to vendor a copy of the script per repo or reference the hub copy. A copy per repo is more robust, since the engine repos should not require a hub checkout to pass their own CI, but then the four copies must be kept in sync.

Refs zerostack-sg3, zerostack-9g4.

title: artifact cleanup can delete the active CodeMode backend and take zero.token offline
description: Observed live 2026-07-25 while following the requirement to periodically clear stale build artifacts. Removing <home>/AI/TokenZero/target also removed target/release/tokenzero, which the active pi-zerostack CodeMode session was using as its zero.token backend. backend_status immediately reported tokenzero:null; subsequent zero.token ref expansion failed with env path missing. The separately installed ~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero remained healthy, so this is backend lifecycle coupling, not source corruption. Deliverables: (1) active backend binaries must live in a protected origin-main runtime directory, never a developer target dir eligible for cleanup; (2) cleanup tooling must detect and refuse active backend paths; (3) backend_status should report the configured path and remediation; (4) regression smoke removes a repo target tree and proves zero.token remains live; (5) document safe stale-artifact cleanup. Recovery today is push origin/main and await backend rebuild.
notes: Investigation refined root cause. The origin-main TokenZero binary is healthy and zero.token shell self-recovered, but backend_status still reports tokenzero:null because router/index.js reads the legacy shared/paths.js TOKENZERO developer-target constant instead of SUBSTRATES.token.binary(). Ref expansion also calls the legacy TOKENZERO constant in router/lib/refs.js, producing ref_not_found env errors after developer target cleanup even while the managed CodeMode child is healthy. Canonical source is currently only in unversioned <home>/Developer/pi-stack/packages/pi-zerostack and <home>/Developer/omp-extensions/omp-backend-router; no pi-zerostack git repo or origin exists, so a durable separate commit cannot be shipped from the four requested repos. Required fix: inject SUBSTRATES.token.binary into createRefHelpers and derive backend_status paths from SUBSTRATES. Reopened until canonical extension ownership is available.
close_reason: Root cause was binary-resolution precedence in the pi-zerostack extension: shared/paths.js ranked ~/AI/<repo>/target/release ahead of protected install prefixes, so the active CodeMode backend routinely resolved into a cleanup-eligible developer artifact tree. Pruning that tree deleted the running binary. Confirmed live before the fix: backend_status reported fszero=~/AI/FSZero/target/release/fszero and gzero=~/AI/graphzero/target/release/graphzero. Fixed in ~/Developer/pi-stack commit f81ba36: (1) backendBinaryCandidates() puts protected prefixes (~/.tokenzero/bin, ~/.fszero/bin, ~/.graphzero/bin, ~/.local/bin) first, developer targets remain a from-source fallback; (2) backend_status now reports artifact_cleanup_safety naming any backend still in target/ plus remediation, so pruning is a checked operation; (3) README documents the safe prune sequence. Verified: all four backends now resolve to protected paths (~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero, ~/.local/bin/fszero, ~/.local/bin/graphzero); new router/test/backend-paths.test.mjs reproduces the exact incident (create both binaries, rm -rf the target tree, assert the resolved backend is unchanged and still exists) and covers both branches of the safety report; mutation-testing both the candidate ordering and the safety filter turns the suite red; full pi-zerostack suite 169/169. pi-stack is a git repo so this is durably committed.

title: shell repo-inventory heuristic mangles compound commands, shredding file content into sample_paths
description:
Hit repeatedly while doing conformance work on 2026-07-25. Not a blocker, but it costs a wasted round trip almost every time and will do the same to every future agent.

zero.token.shell wraps some commands in a "structured (repo inventory command)" policy that reformats output into a repo_inventory block with files_seen/dirs_seen/sample_paths. That is useful for a bare ls. It is actively wrong when the command is a compound shell line whose real payload is on stdout.

Concrete case:
  zero.token.shell("ls /tmp/qs/probe-reports/ && cat /tmp/qs/probe-reports/$(ls ... | head -1)")
The heuristic saw a leading ls, classified the whole thing as repo inventory, and then rendered the JSON report I actually wanted as "sample_paths" entries, one array element per LINE of JSON:
  - gz-2026-07-25-050508.json
  - "contract_version": "1.0",
  - "invalid CodeMode ref \"gz://...\"",
  - "name": "ctx.step",
So the file content was shredded into a path list. Every line got treated as a filesystem path. I had to re-fetch via the combined_ref to read it.

Second case, same root cause: an ls of two paths where the second does not exist returns exit 1 and the stderr line
  ls: /path: No such file or directory
appears as a sample_paths ENTRY, alongside real -rwxr-xr-x lines. A consumer parsing sample_paths as paths gets an error message as a path.

Suggested fix, roughly in order of value:
1. Only apply the inventory policy when the command is a SINGLE listing command with no &&, ||, ;, or | and no command substitution. A compound line should fall through to plain capture.
2. Never route stderr into sample_paths. Inventory is a stdout concept.
3. When the policy is applied, still make the raw stdout trivially reachable; today combined_ref works but it is a second round trip that the caller did not know they needed until they saw mangled output.

Impact is mild but constant: it silently corrupts the shape of data you asked for, and it does so most often when an agent is reading evidence files, which is exactly when fidelity matters. Filed rather than worked around, per the standing instruction to report ZeroStack problems as beads.
close_reason: Independently re-verified on the live origin-main binary TokenZero 78a9a12 from a fresh session. Compound commands with a leading listing are no longer classified as repo inventory and return the payload verbatim. Listing a real and a missing path still classifies as inventory but sample paths now contains only the real entry, with the stderr diagnostic excluded. Bare single listings are still classified as inventory as intended. Fixed in TokenZero 7bada5e.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
VERIFIED LIVE on the rebuilt origin/main binary (TokenZero 78a9a12, built 05:25).

Before, the exact command that motivated this bead shredded the JSON body into sample_paths, one entry per line:
  ls /tmp/qs/probe-reports/ && cat /tmp/qs/probe-reports/<f>
  -> repo_inventory: sample_paths: - "contract_version": "1.0", - "name": "ctx.step", ...

After, the same shape returns the payload verbatim:
  ls /tmp/qs/probe2/ && cat /tmp/qs/probe2/<f> | head -20
  -> gz-2026-07-25-050713.json
     {
       "ns": "gz",
       "bin": "graphzero-codemode + graphzero",
       ...
  No repo_inventory wrapper, no sample_paths, content readable in one call.

stderr fix also verified:
  ls -la <real> <missing>
  -> files_seen: 1, sample_paths contains ONLY the real entry.
  The "No such file or directory" line no longer appears as a path.
  Note that ls ... 2>&1 still shows the diagnostic, correctly: the redirect
  merges the streams in the shell before the renderer ever sees them, so
  there is nothing to separate at that point. Out of scope for this fix.

Fixed in TokenZero 7bada5e, on origin/main.

Caveat worth recording: verifying this required manually fetching and rebuilding the live checkout, because the origin/main backend refresh is stuck. Filed as zerostack-9jj. Without that manual step a push does NOT reach the live surface, and I would have "verified" against a two-day-old binary.

title: TokenZero shared store has no project namespacing: unrelated projects collide on one path
description:
This is the only divergence in the store-root triplicate that puts DIFFERENT objects at the SAME path, rather than the same object at different paths.

TokenZero/crates/tokenzero-engine/src/workspace.rs:106-124 always resolves to <store>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json with no project key. N unrelated projects sharing one ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT all write that same file. workspace.rs:203-216 only emits a store_project_mismatch warning in the resolution report; nothing prevents the collision.

The other two namespace correctly when the store is outside the repo:
- GraphZero: <store>/projects/<project_key>/graphzero/ (zerostack_store.rs:114-123)
- FSZero: <store>/fszero/repos/<sid>/ (zerostack_store.rs:56-62)

Recommended canonical shape is GraphZeros: <root>/projects/<key>/<engine>, with the key being 16 lowercase hex chars of sha256 over the absolutized root path, no prefix. FSZeros sid- prefix belongs at the directory level, not in the key; keeping prefixes means no engine can predict another engines shard directory (FSZero sid-<16hex> = 20 chars vs GraphZero <16hex> = 16).

Also: key input bytes diverge. FSZero uses fs::canonicalize or the path as-given without absolutizing (zerostack_store.rs:100-105); GraphZero absolutizes against cwd when the path does not exist (store/path_safety.rs:35-45). For a nonexistent relative repo_root, FSZero hashes "rel/path" and GraphZero hashes "<cwd>/rel/path", producing different keys for the same repo.

Migration: TokenZero gains namespacing, <pin>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json moves to <pin>/projects/<key>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json. FSZero moves fszero/repos/<sid>/ to projects/<key>/fszero/. GraphZero unchanged.

Anti-collision gate: two distinct roots sharing one pin must resolve to different engine dirs. That test fails against TokenZero today.

Part of zerostack-sce part B.
notes: 2026-07-28 audit: blocked on parent zerostack-sce establishing the canonical shared store-root/project-key contract before cross-engine migration. Implementing TokenZero/FSZero paths first would entrench another divergent layout.

title: EPIC: Cut zero-store CAS cyclomatic density (put/list/atomic)
description:
## Goal
Lower cyclomatic density of zero-store CAS publish paths (`put_with_limit`, `list_objects`, `atomic_write_file`) under hard ceiling CC≤10 without changing CAS durability or race semantics; keep joint ΣCC non-increasing.

## Why (leverage)
Baseline 20260727-repo-sweep-r1: cluster hotspot ΣCC=43 (put 18 + list 12 + atomic 13). Highest product-path risk in the hub joint. Concurrent publish + fsync-before-replace + race converge are load-bearing.

## Risk class
high — Evidence tier: targeted `cargo test -p zero-store` only (never workspace). Human review: required on put/atomic transforms.

## Context (repo anchors)
- Books: `.cut-branches/runs/20260727-repo-sweep-r1/` (LATEST)
- Cards: `04-analysis-cards/{put_with_limit,list_objects,atomic_write_file}.md`
- Waves: `waves/wave1-zero-store-classifier.md`, `wave2-metric-gaming-posture.md`, `wave2-correctness-preflight.md`
- Files: `crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/fs_replace.rs`
- Baseline: ΣCC joint=1071; analyzer lizard 1.23.0

## Current state (as-is)
`put_with_limit` packs size policy, dedup, fan-out dir ensure, temp write, atomic replace, race converge in one CC=18 body. `list_objects` filters walk paths (CC=12). `atomic_write_file` owns unique temp + write/sync/replace (CC=13).

## Desired state (to-be)
Parent functions ≤6–8 CC via named stage extracts; helpers ≤8; no public API change; race converge short-circuit `dest.is_file() && read_verified_at(...).is_ok()` preserved; fsync before replace preserved.

## Spec
### Behavior
1. Shall preserve exact CAS identity, size limits, PolicyDenied, Io error classes.
2. Shall not change concurrent-writer converge behavior.
3. Shall not scatter essential durability rules into untested micro-helpers (metric gaming ban).
### Interfaces
Public crate APIs stable unless separate auth.

## Constraints / bounds
- May edit: `crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/fs_replace.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/**` tests
- Must not: full workspace cargo test; engine private trees; drive-by renames
- Technique: extract method (staged); combine predicates on list_objects
- File lock: `ZeroStack/crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs` sequential; `fs_replace.rs` for atomic
- Stop if: >5 files or ΣCC rises without justified displacement

## Size / limits / deps
- Children: list_objects → atomic_write_file (add tests first) → put_with_limit
- Depends on: transform authorization + targeted crate test allowance
- Blocks: none outside cut-branches queue

## Adversarial / edge cases
1. Concurrent identical put: both writers converge, no double-body corruption
2. Non-NotFound stat errors surface as Io (not silent create)
3. Symlink substitution on fan-out dirs refused
4. atomic_write_file: crash between write and replace leaves no torn dest
5. list_objects: skip non-regular / filter predicates truth table stable

## Acceptance (`done_when`)
- [ ] Each of put_with_limit, list_objects, atomic_write_file re-measured CC≤10 OR blocked_with_reason on card residual
- [ ] Joint or crate-scope ΣCC not increased (re-run measure_complexity.py on crates/zero-store)
- [ ] `cargo test -p zero-store --lib` green (targeted only)
- [ ] Metric-gaming auditor clean on the edit pass (no single-use CC=1 wrapper spam)
- [ ] Analysis cards updated with after CC
- [ ] Fail if full cargo workspace suite was the only proof

## Verify
```bash
# from ZeroStack root — targeted only
python3 ~/AI/JeffreySkills/_custom/cyclomatic-reduction/scripts/measure_complexity.py crates/zero-store --threshold 10 --output /tmp/zs-store-after.json
# compare total_cc to baseline part; use session scratch not shared /tmp in agent runs
cargo test -p zero-store --lib
```
Evidence: after JSON + test log + metric-gaming note.

## Out of scope
Engine CAS copies; GC sweep redesign; public ABI of engines.

## Handoff
Close children first; leave epic open until all three ≤ceiling or blocked. Point residual to NEXT_PASS. Campaign books under `.cut-branches/LATEST`.

description:

title: GraphZero execute_code envelope lacks execution_id and inline telemetry the contract requires
description:
Found by the first live conformance run after the harness was repaired (ZeroStack 2241b75, plus the payload-extraction fix). G2 refs, G3 telemetry, G6 ctx.step, and G9 coalescing all FAIL against GraphZero, and unlike G5/G10 these are NOT harness bugs.

CONTRACT.md section on {ns}_execute_code specifies the success envelope:
  { "ack": "C",
    "execution_id": "cm://exec/1782920000000-012345abcdef",
    "refs": { "code":..., "steps":..., "telemetry":..., "result":... },
    "telemetry": { "kind": "codemode.execute", "status": "ok", "logical_ops":...,
                   "physical_ops":..., "wall_ms":..., ... } }

GraphZero actually returns (verified by direct stdio invocation of
target/release/graphzero-codemode, plan "return 1+1;", form js):
  structuredContent top-level keys: ["ack", "ref", "refs", "value"]
  ack   = "ok gz2 96% t:q:7149bee088e3c5a9"
  ref   = "gz://codemode/execution/cm___exec_1784970487262-50629-0-aae1dac37219/result"
  refs  = [ gz://blob/<64hex>, .../<id>, .../<id>/steps, .../<id>/telemetry, .../<id>/result ]
  value = { ack: "C", ref: "gz://blob/...", value: 2 }

Three concrete divergences:

1. NO execution_id field. The contract wants a top-level execution_id of the form cm://exec/<id>. GraphZero embeds the id only inside ref/refs strings, spelled cm___exec_1784970487262-50629-0-aae1dac37219 (triple underscore, not cm://exec/). A consumer cannot read the execution id without string-parsing a ref, and the id spelling itself differs from the contract's.

2. NO inline telemetry object. The contract wants telemetry inline in the response. GraphZero returns only a gz://.../telemetry REF, requiring a second round trip. This is defensible as a ref-first design and may well be the better shape, but it is not what the contract says, and G3/G9 cannot pass as written. Note G9 coalescing specifically needs telemetry counters to observe batching, so a ref-only telemetry makes that check impossible without an expand step the harness does not do.

3. ack is not "C". The contract shows ack "C" on success; GraphZero returns "ok gz2 96% t:q:<hash>" at the envelope level and puts ack "C" one level down in value. So the contract's shape appears at value, not at the top.

Note GraphZero looks INTERNALLY consistent and arguably richer than the contract; this reads as the contract having been written against an older or different envelope and never reconciled, rather than as a regression. That is exactly the "closed-but-unproven" state zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a flagged: GraphZero closed zeroref-v1-shared-cas-1ghi.8/.9 as done while its own evidence file stayed pending.

Needs a contract owner decision, same as zerostack-g25:
A. The contract is normative and GraphZero must add execution_id and inline telemetry.
B. The ref-first envelope is correct and CONTRACT.md plus the harness must be updated to match, with telemetry expansion added to G3/G9.

Do not guess. Whichever way it goes, TokenZero and FSZero must be checked for the same divergence before a shared answer is written down, since the contract is supposed to be cross-engine.

Related: zerostack-hix (harness), zerostack-g25 (mutation vocabulary), zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a (parent).

title: RCH active-project exclusion silently falls back to local compilation
description: Observed live 2026-07-25. RCH_VISIBILITY=verbose rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_zerostack cargo test -p zero-store --all-targets returned exit 0 but printed `[RCH] local (no admissible workers: active_project_exclusion=1)` and compiled locally while another ZeroStack clippy job occupied spark-1672. This violates remote-only build policy and can exhaust the Mac while looking successful. Deliverables: (1) add a strict remote-only mode or env that errors instead of fail-open; (2) pi/rch workflow uses strict mode for all builds/tests; (3) active-project exclusion should queue or return structured busy, not run locally; (4) regression test proves no local compiler process starts; (5) telemetry distinguishes remote success, queued/busy, and forbidden local fallback.
notes: BLOCKED-ON-DECISION 2026-07-28: rch is upstream binary-only (brew tap dicklesworthstone/tap, github.com/Dicklesworthstone/remote_compilation_helper, no local source anywhere on this machine; binary self-updates). Fixing requires either (a) upstream issue/PR for RCH_STRICT_REMOTE fail-closed mode, (b) local fork = toolchain-ownership change needing operator sign-off, or (c) interim band-aid guard that fails on '[RCH] local' in verbose output. Full analysis: /tmp/racc_run/opus-rch-strict.md

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, with the exact log line, while verifying fszero-ixka.

rch fail-opens to local compilation for any project whose path resolves outside its canonical
root (~). A clean checkout at /tmp/ixka-clean produced, from rch/src/hook.rs:1691:

  WARN rch::hook: Project path normalization failed for /private/tmp/ixka-clean:
  input resolves outside canonical root (input: /private/tmp/ixka-clean, detail:
  resolved=/private/tmp/ixka-clean root=~)

and then every build printed "[RCH] local (remote execution failed)" while still SUCCEEDING,
so the only visible symptom was that a 9-minute release build ran on the laptop instead of the
20-core worker. Note /tmp -> /private/tmp on macOS: the symlink resolution is what pushes it
outside the root, so the path an agent types is not the path rch judges.

Two things make this worse than a normal fallback:
1. The message says "remote execution failed", which is false and misdirects diagnosis toward
   the worker, SSH, and the build itself. The remote was never attempted.
2. 'rch diagnose --dry-run' on the SAME path reports "Would offload: YES (compilation command
   meets threshold, worker available)" and lists all six pipeline steps as [RUN]. So the
   documented diagnostic tool contradicts the actual behavior for this cause. Only the WARN
   line, which is not part of the [RCH] contract output, tells the truth.

PROOF: re-cloning the identical tree to ~/ixka-clean and running the identical
command produced "[RCH] remote spark-1672" with real offload and artifact retrieval.

Suggested acceptance: the fail-open reason must name the actual cause ("project outside rch
canonical root <root>") rather than "remote execution failed", and 'rch diagnose' must report
NO for a path it will refuse, rather than YES.

title: CAS temp-file reapers are mutually blind: each engine leaks the others temp files forever
description:
Three temp-file naming schemes and two mutually exclusive reap predicates, so abandoned temps from a crashed publisher are never cleaned by a different engine sharing the store.

Names:
- hub ZeroStack/crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs:197 and GraphZero .../shared_cas.rs:141 -> .tmp-<hash[..8]>-<pid>-<seq>
- TokenZero .../shared_cas.rs:87 -> .tmp-<hash64>-<nanos>-<n>.blob
- FSZero src/core/cas.rs:231-238 -> <hash64>.<pid>.<seq>.tmp

Reap predicates:
- hub cas.rs:300-320 and GraphZero :251 match PREFIX ".tmp-", age >= 3600s
- FSZero cas.rs:281-291 matches SUFFIX ".tmp", age >= 900s
- TokenZero has no reaper at all

title: uncommitted TokenZero duplicate of VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION will fail CI and reopens tokenzero-rnv2
description:
Found while investigating zerostack-spz part 1. Reported by Agent Mail with ack requested, filed as a bead so it survives an unread inbox.

WHERE
crates/tokenzero-core/src/tokens.rs:37, UNCOMMITTED, on branch harness-no-host-paths, in another session's working tree (81 files dirty at the time of filing).

WHAT
  const LOSSY_VISIBLE_BUDGET_MARKER: &str = "[mode=lossy lossy_policy_id=tokenzero.visible-compression.v1 lossy_spans=[{description=omitted-bytes reason=visible-budget recovery_may_be_needed=true}]]";
It is a byte-identical duplicate of pub const VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION two lines above it, at line 35, and it has zero callers. grep across the workspace returns exactly one hit: the definition.

IMPACT
  cargo build -p tokenzero-core
  warning: constant `LOSSY_VISIBLE_BUDGET_MARKER` is never used
  warning: `tokenzero-core` (lib) generated 1 warning
TokenZero CI runs clippy with -D warnings, so this becomes a hard build failure the moment it is committed.

WHY IT IS A REGRESSION AND NOT MERELY DEAD CODE
tokenzero-rnv2 was closed for fixing exactly this. Its fix (5d82ea2) collapsed three duplicated copies of this string into a single pub const, because a divergent copy was the root cause of the visible-budget test failing invariant P01-001: the test modelled a 14-token marker while the emitted marker costs 33, so with budget=17 the marker alone exceeded the budget and only the footer could be emitted.

Verified origin/main is clean: it contains only the declaration at line 35 and its single use at line 51, with no second constant. So the duplicate was reintroduced locally AFTER the fix landed. If it is committed, rnv2 reopens, and the failure mode it reintroduces is the metadata displacing the payload it describes.

FIX
Delete line 37. Do not wire anything to it. Every call site should keep using VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION, which is documented in place as the single source of truth precisely to prevent this.

NOT DONE BY ME, deliberately: the file is another session's uncommitted work, and editing an 81-file dirty tree underneath a live session risks destroying it. That already happened once today in this repo (zerostack-wth). Owner should delete it before committing.

Also blocks zerostack-spz part 1, whose fix lives in enforce_token_budget_with_ref in this same file.ZEOF
wc -c /tmp/az/dup.txt
close_reason: Resolved. The callerless duplicate LOSSY_VISIBLE_BUDGET_MARKER is gone from crates/tokenzero-core/src/tokens.rs; grep across the workspace returns zero hits, and 'cargo build -p tokenzero-core' emits no unused-constant warning, so the hard failure this bead predicted under CI's 'cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings' cannot occur. Found a second, related problem while verifying: this branch's HEAD had ALSO lost pub const VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION itself and re-inlined the literal at its only use, locally undoing the rnv2 fix 5d82ea2 (origin/main has the constant twice: definition plus use; this branch's HEAD had it zero times). Removing the duplicate alone would have left the branch one inline literal away from re-diverging, so I restored the constant with the doc comment recording why it must stay single. Committed as 53b46f6. The rnv2 failure mode cannot reappear through the tests either: both test sites (tokens_inline_tests.rs:45 and lib.rs:407) reference VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION rather than carrying their own literal, which is exactly the divergence that made the budget test model a 14-token marker against a real 33-token one and let the metadata displace its payload. Verified: tokenzero-core tests 88/4/7 pass. Five too_many_arguments clippy errors in operation_abi/registry.rs are pre-existing, present at origin/main, untouched by this change, and out of scope here.

title: store-root resolution: FSZero inverts precedence and has no shared-store opt-in gate
description:
Two engines resolve the same repo to different store roots, so a single logical store silently splits.

FSZero/src/core/zerostack_store.rs:20-27 checks the env pin FIRST and has no opt-in gate:
  if let Some(v) = env(ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT).or(ZERO_STACK_STORE_ROOT) { return Some(...) }
  let candidate = repo_root.join(".zerostack"); if candidate.is_dir() { Some(candidate) } else { None }

TokenZero/crates/tokenzero-engine/src/workspace.rs:77-95 and GraphZero/crates/graphzero-store/src/store/zerostack_store.rs:91-112 both check local .zerostack FIRST, then require a shared-store opt-in before honoring the pin.

Consequences:
- Repo with .zerostack present plus ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT=/shared and no opt-in: FSZero writes /shared/fszero/repos/<sid>/, TokenZero and GraphZero write <repo>/.zerostack/.
- Bare ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT with no .zerostack: FSZero honors it, the other two ignore it.
- FSZERO_SHARED_STORE does not exist anywhere in FSZero source. Only a doc mention of ZEROSTACK_SHARED_STORE at FSZero/docs/design/zeroref-v1-annex.md:152. Adding it is a new surface, not a rename.

Recommended canonical behavior, 2 of 3 majority: local .zerostack wins over the pin, and the pin requires opt-in. The local marker is an explicit per-repo declaration; a process-global env is ambient and a stray value in an agent harness should not relocate one engines store.

Migration: FSZero only. Repos with both .zerostack and a pin move <pin>/fszero/{store.sqlite3,repos/<sid>/store.sqlite3} to <repo>/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3. FSZero already has the machinery at src/core/store_migration.rs:87-100. With a bare ungated pin, FSZero returns to <repo>/.fszero/store.sqlite3, which looks like data loss to existing users, so ship FSZERO_SHARED_STORE plus a one-shot migration that adopts the old ungated location.

Part of zerostack-sce part B.
close_reason: FSZero now uses the two-of-three canonical order. src/core/zerostack_store.rs gained resolve_store_root_with_env with the same rule TokenZero (workspace.rs:79) and GraphZero (zerostack_store.rs:91) already share: local .zerostack wins, then the pin, and only when opted in. Added FSZERO_SHARED_STORE / ZEROSTACK_SHARED_STORE with the same truthy set (1|on|true|yes, trimmed, case-insensitive) and the same empty-pin filter. Commit 3093e45 in FSZero; docs corrected in a3fc479 (shared-cas.md named the old precedence outright; README.md and mcp.md implied a bare pin sufficed). Migration shipped as required, because the precedence fix alone strands data in exactly the two cases the bead names: repo with both .zerostack and a pin, and a bare ungated pin (which now falls back to legacy .fszero and would look like data loss). adopt_superseded_store runs from prepare_repo_store before the DB is opened, using superseded_store_root to name where the OLD resolver would have looked, and moves the DB there to the location the new resolver names. Safety properties, each pinned by a test AND mutation-verified by breaking it and confirming the specific test goes red: never overwrites (conflict reported, both DBs preserved, since merging two live databases is not a decision it can make); copy-then-remove rather than rename, because the pin is usually on another filesystem where rename fails EXDEV; staged into the destination dir then renamed, so a crash leaves the untouched source or a complete destination, never a half-written DB; -wal/-shm move with the DB, since a stranded -wal holds committed-but-uncheckpointed transactions; inert when source and destination coincide. Verified: 11 new tests in tests/zerostack_store_pi1.rs pass. Reverting the resolver to the pin-first ungated order turns all 6 precedence tests red including the bead's exact scenario. precedence_matches_the_canonical_cross_engine_table asserts all 8 combinations of (local, pin, opt-in) so a future one-off tweak to any branch surfaces as a diff rather than silent drift. Suite-wide the failure set is IDENTICAL before and after: 9 failures, all pre-existing (lib codemode accounting x2, batch_ops, cas, cas_migration x2, child_root x5), confirmed by stashing the change and rerunning the same four suites. No new rustfmt drift.

title: EPIC: RACC Exact Causal Frontier realization (proof-carrying compression across the hub)
description:
## Goal
Realize the RACC Exact Causal Frontier paper as ZeroStack hub crates + conformance so TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero inherit proof-carrying zero-degradation compression from one base. Paper vendored at docs/racc/RACC_EXACT_CAUSAL_FRONTIER_V1.md; reference Rust contract at docs/racc/RACC_CONTRACT.rs (commit these with the first tier-1 child).

## Locked architecture decisions
1. Hub owns MECHANISM: types, certificate verify, ledger arithmetic, gate state machine, conformance suites.
2. Engines/host own POLICY: driving loops, I/O, retries, expansion timing (rustls model: crate owns protocol state machine, caller owns sockets).
3. Performance laws (conformance-enforced): no RACC operation may add a round trip (certificates travel inline with the payload they certify); hub crates are sync, no-I/O, allocation-free on hot paths; verify() on resident objects is a 32-byte digest compare; certificates are built at write time in the same pass that hashes for CAS; certificate results are memoizable by (object_digest, index_version).

## Crate map (paper section 11.2 -> hub)
| paper module | invariant | home |
| archive | immutable byte-exact recovery | zero-store (extend) |
| object_id/span | digest-bound identity+range | zero-ref v2 (extend) |
| certificate+verify | exact payload, provenance, completeness witness | zero-cert (NEW) |
| ledger | locked tokenizer, every call charged, T8 replay identity | zero-ledger (NEW) |
| router | nested monotone budgets, geometric doubling, factor 4 | zero-gate (NEW) |
| receipt | machine-checkable exact_phase_valid | zero-ledger + conformance |
| transaction | clone/verify/commit-or-rollback (T13) | engine/host, tracked here |
| fallback | exact raw before irreversible action | zero-gate + zero-abi effect machinery |

## Theorem constraints (violating any of these is a bug)
- T6 (undecidability): never certify semantic sufficiency of a summary. Only mechanical facts are certifiable: byte identity/range, exact-search completeness over a locked byte domain, all-references/graph closure under a locked parser+index version, token counts under a locked tokenizer, build/test outcomes in immutable envs, exposure/retry/fallback accounting, the final C<=epsilon*R inequality. Everything else routes TaskVerified or RawFallback.
- T5: no universal compression-ratio claims anywhere (docs, telemetry, marketing). Targets are task-indexed phases: C<=epsilon*R => saving >= 1-epsilon.
- T10/T11: online expansion is deterministic geometric 4-competitive; certificate selection is heuristic (NP-hard) and must never be described as minimal.

## done_when
- [ ] Tier-1 children closed: zero-cert, zero-ref v2 span digests, zero-store ingest metadata, zero-ledger, zero-gate, RACC conformance
- [ ] Engine adoption children (fz/gz/tz) + T13 transactional verifier gate closed
- [ ] RADC-D telemetry child producing beta-exponent and phase data
- [ ] Release gate met (paper 12.2): 100% byte recovery for resident objects; 100% certified typed-query correctness; no demonstrated task regression; complete fallback/retry accounting; preregistered phase target (e.g. C/R<=0.03)
notes: REVIEW FIX (worker-sol, BLOCKER): epic line 'verify() on resident objects is a 32-byte digest compare' is unsound as stated — cold verification must check the full certificate; cached success may use constant-size compares ONLY when keyed by (certificate_digest, verifier_version, locked_operator/domain_version), never (object_digest,index_version) alone which aliases queries. Also: release gate must restore paper 12.2 VERBATIM ('no statistically or transactionally demonstrated task regression') — see .6 notes. Review report: /tmp/racc_run/sol-review.md

title: feat(zero-cert): evidence certificates, completeness witnesses, sound verify (T2/T6/T14)
description:
## Goal
New hub crate crates/zero-cert: the RACC evidence-certificate core. Types from paper 11.1 (docs/racc/RACC_CONTRACT.rs is the reference source, ~200 lines, adapt not copy-paste): SpanRef{object_id,byte_start,byte_len,object_digest,span_digest}, Query enum (ReadSpan, ExactSearch, Definition, References, AstClosure, CallPath, DataflowSlice, Diff, BuildReceipt, TestTrace), Provenance (incl. parser/index version pins), CompletenessWitness, EvidenceCertificate{query,spans,payload,provenance,completeness,input_token_cost,backend_work_units}, VerifiedEvidence newtype, plus pure fn verify(&EvidenceCertificate, resolver) -> Result<VerifiedEvidence, VerificationError>.

## Why
T2/T14: universal zero degradation holds only if every committed compressed decision has a SOUND sufficiency certificate. Soundness must live once in the hub so a verifier bug is fixed once and inherited by all three engines. This crate is the critical path for every other RACC bead.

## Spec
1. VerifiedEvidence is constructible ONLY via verify() (private field; enforce with a test that the type cannot be built outside the crate).
2. verify() checks: span digests match payload bytes; object digests match declared identity; completeness witness is well-formed for the query kind under the DECLARED (locked) operator version. It must never accept a witness kind for a query kind it does not match.
3. T6 boundary in the type system: there is NO witness variant for semantic summary sufficiency. Do not add one.
4. Wire format: serde + zero-abi canonical JSON for digest-stable encoding. Depend on zero-abi (digest helpers) and zero-ref (hash/hex). Do NOT touch zero-abi/raw_worker.rs (dirty, prior campaign).
5. Perf: sync, #![forbid(unsafe_code)], no I/O, zero allocation in verify() hot path when payload is borrowed; digest compare is constant-time-irrelevant memcmp of [u8;32].

## Constraints
- New crate + one-line workspace member addition only; no edits to existing dirty files.
- Follow zero-abi crate layout conventions (lib.rs module tree, golden-vector tests).
- Build/test via RCH remote policy: rch exec -- cargo test -p zero-cert

## done_when
- [ ] Crate compiles under workspace; forbid(unsafe_code)
- [ ] Golden vectors: valid certificate accepted; tampered payload byte, tampered span range, wrong witness kind, stale operator version each rejected with typed error
- [ ] Property test: for random payloads, verify(make_certificate(p)) always accepts and any single-bit mutation of payload or digest rejects
- [ ] Privacy test proving VerifiedEvidence unconstructable externally
- [ ] Criterion bench recorded in .bench-history: verify() resident-object path; assert no alloc (allocation-counting test)

## Verify
rch exec -- cargo test -p zero-cert
rch exec -- cargo check -p zero-cert

## Anti-goals
No I/O or CAS access inside this crate (resolver is a trait the caller implements); no async; no semantic-sufficiency witness variant; no engine-specific query kinds.
notes: REVIEW FINDING (worker-sol, HIGH) for implementer: 'witness is well-formed' is too weak — verify witness TRUTH against resolver-owned immutable domain/operator state: range bounds, canonical ordered payload/span mapping, all digests, query parameters, exhaustive completeness, exact locked version. Declarations are not self-authenticating. Add omission tests: drop one real search match / reference / closure node / span for every supported Query-to-witness mapping; verifier must reject each.
close_reason: Added zero-cert with trusted version locks, query-bound mechanical completeness witnesses, canonical wire digests, private verified evidence, allocation-free resident verification, golden/property/privacy tests, and Criterion benchmark. Final targeted test and benchmark passed remotely on spark-1672. Vendored the epic's RACC reference artifacts. [commit cf6e4512bc749a645506fc3a4abbcc09515ed163]

title: feat(transaction): T13 task-verified speculation — TaskAcceptanceReceipt, verify-commit-or-rollback
description:
## Goal
T13 transactional verifier branch: task-success no-regret speculation. When pre-action certification is unavailable (T6 boundary), the runtime may attempt the task in a sandbox and commit ONLY on objective verification (tests/build receipts), else roll back to raw. Hub-side: define the TaskAcceptanceReceipt contract and the conformance gate; host/engine-side: wire FSZero TransactionJournal + build/test execution as the verifier.

## Why
Theorem 8.2: sandboxed verification + raw rollback is task-success non-regressive — the transactional branch can NEVER make outcomes worse, only cheaper. It is the legal escape hatch for everything mechanical certification cannot cover, and the branch most coding tasks will actually use (fix-until-tests-pass is exactly this shape).

## Spec
1. TaskAcceptanceReceipt (hub type, zero-gate or zero-cert): verifier command identity (CommandId + env digest), outcome, artifact digests, journal id. Receipt only constructible from an actual verifier run (same constructibility-privacy pattern as VerifiedEvidence).
2. Verifier must be transactional per CONTRACT.md TransactionJournal reference behavior: any commit path without a passing receipt must roll back. Paper Def 8.1: verifier acceptance must be objective and machine-checkable (exit codes + expected artifact digests), never model-judged.
3. Failed speculation cost is charged to the ledger (c_attempt in RADC-D premise 10.3) — speculation is never free in accounting even when rolled back.
4. Irreversible external effects (network, deletes outside journal scope) are NOT speculatable — the gate must refuse the transactional branch for those effect classes.

## done_when
- [ ] TaskAcceptanceReceipt type + constructibility privacy landed in a hub crate
- [ ] Conformance gate: scripted failing-verifier speculation rolls back and reports the attempt in receipt accounting; passing-verifier speculation commits with receipt
- [ ] Host-side driving-loop bead filed (pi-zerostack / CodeMode host) and linked via external_ref
- [ ] Effect-class refusal tested: irreversible effect + speculation request = typed rejection

## Anti-goals
No model-as-judge verification; no free speculation (all attempts charged); no speculation on irreversible effect classes.

title: task(radc-d): falsifier telemetry, beta-exponent regression, preregistered phase targets
description:
## Goal
RADC-D experimental program: telemetry and analysis deciding whether the conjecture premises (10.1 sublinear causal width, 10.2 bounded hierarchy quality, 10.3 low fallback / high verifier acceptance) hold on real ZeroStack workloads. The implication premises => savings -> 1 is proved; whether OUR workloads satisfy the premises is empirical, with explicit falsifiers.

## Telemetry to collect (from zero-ledger receipts + gate transcripts, per session)
R (raw accountability), C (RACC-visible communication), K_H proxy (certified-view sizes), fallback frequency and cost, verifier acceptance p, c_attempt, re-expansion multiplicity per ref, certificate cache hit rate, backend work units.

## Analyses (paper 12.3)
1. log K vs log R regression -> causal-width exponent beta with confidence bands; premise 10.1 needs beta < 1.
2. Phase surface: C/R distribution per task class; distance to preregistered target C/R <= 0.03.
3. Falsifier dashboard (paper section 10, seven falsifiers), each a named metric with an alarm threshold: (1) K linear in R; (2) hierarchy ratio unbounded; (3) re-expansion multiplicity cancels replay savings; (4) pre-action certificates almost never fire; (5) verifier rejection dominates residual; (6) backend work/latency exceeds token value; (7) fallback not transactional before irreversible actions.

## Preregistration discipline
The target phase (epsilon) is committed in-repo BEFORE data collection per release (paper 12.2 release gate). No post-hoc epsilon shopping. Findings land as committed reports under benchmarks/ following the .bench-history two-pass discipline.

## Constraints
- Depends on zero-ledger and at least one engine adoption bead emitting real receipts.
- Data scrubbed per beads-export privacy gates (no host paths); digests and counts only, no raw content exfiltration.

## done_when
- [ ] Telemetry fields emitted and documented (schema in conformance/schemas or benchmarks/)
- [ ] beta regression + phase surface produced from >=1 real workload corpus, committed with provenance (SHAs, corpus id, machine)
- [ ] Falsifier dashboard with the seven named metrics and thresholds
- [ ] Written verdict per premise: supported / falsified / insufficient data — with specific falsifier evidence either way

## Anti-goals
No cherry-picked corpora; no claiming RADC-D proved (it is a conjecture; only premises-on-workload evidence); no universal-percentage claims (T5).
notes: DASHBOARD ADDITION (Thm 9.5 full Pareto dominance): token dominance alone does not imply latency or backend-compute dominance. Add two explicit dashboard inequalities: (a) backend cost delta < Value(token savings) monetized/resource-normalized (9.11); (b) recovery+verification latency < saved prefill latency. '99.9% token reduction at catastrophic latency is not a Pareto break.' Also: exact target surface form is h + delta/mu <= epsilon (5.11-5.13) where h=exposure ratio, delta=re-expansion overhead, mu=replay multiplicity — report all three components separately so thrashing (delta) is visible, not hidden.

title: task(zero-ledger): accounting completeness + anti-forgery hardening (review follow-up)
description:
## Goal
Harden zero-ledger (delivered in ba11c54) against the four soundness gaps found in spec review — accounting completeness and anti-forgery. Small, targeted changes to crates/zero-ledger/src/lib.rs + tests.

## Why
T8/section 2.2 charge EVERY model-visible call. As delivered, retry/recovery/fallback counters exist but nothing forces them into racc_input_tokens exactly once — ppm can pass while costs hide in side counters. And RetainedFractionPpm/exactness booleans are caller-controlled, so a receipt can be forged trivially.

## Spec
1. Derive racc_input_tokens for receipt purposes as the append-only sum over ALL charge classes (billed + failed trials + retries + verification/recovery + expansions + fallback) under the locked tokenizer; finalize_receipt() must reject unclassified or double-counted calls (typed error). check_replay_identity() verifies paper eq (5.7) with framing/boundary interactions placed in H.
2. Validate RetainedFractionPpm in 0..=1_000_000 at construction AND serde deserialization (reject out-of-range on the wire).
3. meets_token_target()/exact_phase_valid(): require raw_input_tokens > 0 (typed error or explicit false, documented) — R=0 must not certify a phase.
4. Exactness gates (byte_exact, policy_exact_or_fallback, task_verified) must not be freely settable public booleans: constructor takes evidence handles (archive attestation, per-decision policy/fallback receipts, or T13 TaskAcceptanceReceipt once zero-gate lands) or at minimum crate-private setters with a documented trusted-caller boundary. Keep policy-exact receipts distinct from T13 task-no-regret receipts (paper 8.2/8.3, non-claim 14.9).

## done_when
- [ ] One omission-mutation test per charge class: hiding that class from the receipt sum must fail finalize or the gate
- [ ] Serde rejects ppm > 1_000_000; construction rejects too
- [ ] R=0 cannot produce exact_phase_valid()==true
- [ ] Public API cannot forge exactness booleans (compile-fail or privacy test)
- [ ] Existing 33 tests still green: rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_zerostack cargo test -p zero-ledger

## Anti-goals
No floats; no breaking the canonical-JSON receipt schema without bumping its version; no full-workspace test runs.
close_reason: Derived racc_input_tokens from all six charge classes with typed unclassified/double-counted rejection; range-validated RetainedFractionPpm at construction and deserialization; R=0 can no longer certify a phase; exactness gates now require verified evidence handles. 45/45 targeted tests pass. title: feat(zero-ledger): resource gauge, T8 exposure/replay identity, exact-phase dominance receipt
description:
## Goal
New hub crate crates/zero-ledger: the RACC resource gauge and dominance receipt. Port the arithmetic of docs/racc/RACC_CONTRACT.rs: TokenBudget, RetainedFractionPpm, per-call charging, cumulative counters (raw_input_tokens, racc_input_tokens, recovery/re-expansion tokens, fallback cost, retries), the T8 exposure/replay identity, and DominanceReceipt with meets_token_target() (u128 ppm arithmetic, no floats) and exact_phase_valid().

## Why
T8 (exact exposure/replay identity) and T14 (master phase theorem) turn "percent saved" from marketing into a machine-checkable inequality C<=epsilon*R. TokenZero already emits billed/raw/recovery/visible token counts per call; this crate is the single home for the arithmetic so tz/fz/gz and the CodeMode host all account identically. Fully independent of zero-cert -> parallelize with it.

## Spec
1. Locked-tokenizer identity: LedgerConfig carries tokenizer_id + tokenizer_version_digest; all counts are tagged with it; mixing counts from different tokenizer identities is a typed error (T4/T14 gauge lock).
2. Every charge is append-only and monotone; no API to decrement or rewrite history.
3. T8 identity check: exposure accounting must satisfy the replay identity exactly (see paper section 5, Theorem "exact exposure/replay identity"); provide fn check_replay_identity() used by conformance.
4. Receipt arithmetic exactly as RACC_CONTRACT.rs: lhs = racc_input_tokens * 1_000_000 <= raw_input_tokens * target_retained_ppm, u128 widening, plus byte_exact && policy_exact_or_fallback && task_verified gates.

title: feat(zero-gate): DecisionGate state machine + geometric budgets (T10 factor-4, pure sync)
description:
## Goal
New hub crate crates/zero-gate: the DecisionGate protocol state machine. Enum DecisionGate{Certified(PolicySufficiencyWitness), TaskVerified(TaskAcceptanceReceipt), Expand(NextBudget), RawFallback} plus a pure, synchronous, allocation-free state machine: fn decide(state, input) -> (state, DecisionGate) where input carries certificate-verification outcome (from zero-cert), optional task-acceptance receipt, current budget state, and the pending action's effect class (zero-abi EffectGrant vocabulary).

## Why
T2's universal zero-degradation guarantee is exactly this gate: certified-or-fallback before every committed compressed decision. T10 gives the online expansion law: geometric budget doubling b0*2^k with deterministic factor-4 competitiveness (sharp; Theorem 6.2). Solo-engine installs (tz alone) need the gate too, so it cannot live only in the CodeMode host. Hub owns mechanism; engines/host own the driving loop.

## Spec
1. State machine is TOTAL: every (state,input) pair has a defined transition; no panics; invalid sequences return typed errors, never UB states.
2. Budget schedule: nested monotone expansion, geometric doubling from configurable b0. Cumulative model-visible expansion cost tracked in-state; expose the T10 bound check so conformance can assert cost < 4*K_H + q*(1+ceil(log2(K_H/b0))) for the committed sequence.
3. Irreversibility rule: if effect class is irreversible and there is neither VerifiedEvidence nor TaskAcceptanceReceipt, the ONLY legal output is RawFallback. Make the illegal state unrepresentable (branch selection consumes proof tokens; committing a compressed view requires ownership of VerifiedEvidence or TaskAcceptanceReceipt by construction).
4. Randomization note (paper Remark 6.3) is out of scope: deterministic only.
5. Perf: decide() is pure sync, zero heap allocation (assert via allocation-counting test), no I/O, no async, forbid(unsafe_code).

## Constraints
- Depends on zero-cert types (and zero-abi effect vocabulary read-only). New crate + workspace line only; do not touch dirty zero-abi/raw_worker.rs.
- rch exec -- cargo test -p zero-gate

## done_when
- [ ] Exhaustive transition table tested (proptest over input sequences: no panic, no illegal commit)
- [ ] Adversarial demand sequences (port the geometric/nonmonotone cases exercised by the paper's independent C++ checker, /tmp/racc_v1/RACC_INDEPENDENT_CHECK.cpp semantics) never exceed the factor-4 bound
- [ ] Compile-level proof: committing a compressed view without a proof token does not typecheck (doc-test with compile_fail)
- [ ] Bench in .bench-history: decide() p50 nanosecond-scale, no-alloc assertion

## Verify
rch exec -- cargo test -p zero-gate

## Anti-goals
No engine calls, timeouts, retries, or async in this crate (that is the host loop); no policy heuristics about WHEN to expand beyond the budget law; no nondeterminism.

title: feat(zero-ref): v2 span digests — digest-bound SpanRef without full-object fetch
description:
## Goal
ZeroRef v2: digest-bound spans. Today a (fz|gz|tz)://blob ref binds the WHOLE object digest; a span cannot be verified without fetching the full object. Paper 11.1 SpanRef requires both object_digest and span_digest so span payloads verify in O(32 bytes). Extend zero-ref so span identity is independently verifiable.

## Why
This is the critical-path identity primitive for zero-cert: EvidenceCertificate.spans carry span_digest, and verify() on resident spans becomes a memcmp instead of a full-object hash. Also the enabler for sound cross-session certificate caching keyed by (object_digest, index_version).

## Spec
1. Decision to record as ADR (docs/adr/): whether span_digest lives (a) only in the structured SpanRef type consumed by zero-cert, or (b) also in the ref grammar as an additive v2 fragment (e.g. #B<s>-<e>;sd=<64hex>). Recommendation: (a) first, (b) only if a wire ref must carry it; v1 grammar must remain valid and UNCHANGED either way.
2. span_digest = sha256 of the exact span bytes after CANONICAL_LINE_END_POLICY selection; computed in the SAME pass that hashes the object at write time (no second read).
3. Golden vectors: extend fixtures/zeroref_v1_vectors.json with span-digest vectors; existing v1 vectors must be byte-identical (no digest drift; this is the zerostack-hft lockstep invariant).
4. Coordinate with epic zerostack-hft (identity lockstep) and its clamp matrix; use select_fragment/CANONICAL only.

## Constraints
- BLOCKED: crates/zero-ref/src/lib.rs carries uncommitted prior-campaign edits (see zerostack-jz6i). Do not start until that lands/reconciles.
- rch exec -- cargo test -p zero-ref --test golden_vectors

## done_when
- [ ] ADR committed with the grammar decision and rationale
- [ ] SpanRef type with object_digest + span_digest exported for zero-cert
- [ ] Span-digest golden vectors pass; all pre-existing v1 vectors unchanged
- [ ] Property test: verify-by-span-digest equals verify-by-full-object-hash-then-slice for random objects/spans
- [ ] Single-pass hashing demonstrated (no API requiring a second read of object bytes)

## Verify

rch exec -- cargo test -p zero-ref --test golden_vectors

## Anti-goals
No breaking change to v1 refs; no engine-internal ref grammars absorbed into the hub; no uppercase/short-prefix leniency.

title: feat(zero-store): ObservationMetadata at ingest + named byte-exact residency invariant
description:
## Goal
zero-store as the RACC archive module: (1) ObservationMetadata recorded at ingest (paper 11.5 harness fn ingest(bytes, metadata) -> ObjectId): source engine, session, timestamp, declared kind; stored content-addressed alongside the object without changing object bytes or digests. (2) The release-gate residency property made testable: "100% byte recovery for resident objects" (paper 12.2) as an explicit invariant test: every object accepted by put is byte-identical on get_verified until GC removes it, and removal is observable (typed miss, never silent corruption).

## Why
T3.5 (sound pre-action fallback) requires the archive to be able to render exact raw bytes on demand; the dominance receipt's byte_exact leg rests on this crate. Metadata-at-ingest is what lets certificates carry Provenance without a side lookup (no added round trip).

## Spec
1. Metadata is append-only, keyed by ObjectId, and NOT part of the object digest (byte identity of objects is unchanged; zero digest drift).
2. Residency test: property test over put/get_verified/GC interleavings under the existing StoreLock; any get_verified success returns exactly the ingested bytes (already partially guaranteed; make it an explicit named invariant test suite).
3. Reuse gc_lock and fs_replace primitives; coordinate with epics zerostack-tk7 (durability) and zerostack-sce (CAS convergence) rather than duplicating their scope: this bead adds the metadata surface and the named invariant, not new durability semantics.

- [ ] Named residency invariant suite green (put -> get_verified byte equality; GC'd object -> typed miss)
- [ ] No new fsync barriers on the hot path (coordinate with zerostack-tokenzero-cas-fsync-ovn; do not regress publish latency)

No durability semantics changes (owned by tk7/sce); no metadata mixed into content digests; no second write barrier for metadata on the publish path.

title: feat(conformance): RACC gate suite — certificates, receipts, irreversibility, budgets, inline, residency
description:
## Goal
Extend conformance/ with the RACC gate suite: machine-checkable checks that any substrate claiming RACC conformance (fz/gz/tz, future engines) upholds the theorem invariants. This is the shared-test-suite hub role: engine repos run this suite instead of reimplementing it.

## Checks to implement (each a separate gate id, follow existing G* pattern in conformance/src/checks.rs; coordinate with zerostack-2ae schema unification — do NOT add a third schema style)
1. RACC-CERT: submit golden EvidenceCertificates (valid + tampered set from zero-cert fixtures) through the substrate; valid must verify, tampered must be rejected with typed error. 100% certified typed-query correctness is the release-gate bar (paper 12.2).
2. RACC-RECEIPT: after a scripted plan, substrate emits a DominanceReceipt (zero-ledger schema); check_replay_identity() passes; exact_phase_valid arithmetic recomputed independently by the harness and must match.
3. RACC-GATE-IRREV: a scripted irreversible mutation with no verified evidence must produce RawFallback (never a committed compressed decision). Mutation-test this: a substrate that skips the gate must FAIL the suite.
4. RACC-BUDGET: scripted expansion sequences must respect nested monotone geometric budgets; cumulative expansion cost checked against the factor-4 bound (zero-gate bound checker).
5. RACC-INLINE: certificates must arrive inline with the payload they certify — the harness counts round trips; any flow requiring a second call to fetch a certificate fails (epic performance law).
6. RACC-RESIDENCY: put N objects through the substrate store surface, get_verified all N byte-identical (100% byte recovery for resident objects).

title: feat(adoption/fz): FSZero emits evidence certificates for read/search/diff/mutation receipts
description:
## Goal
FSZero adopts the RACC layer: emit EvidenceCertificates for its mechanically-certifiable operations and pass the hub RACC conformance suite. Implementation lives in the FSZero repo; THIS bead tracks the hub-side contract, the adoption gate, and cross-repo sequencing (file the mirror bead in FSZero when unblocked and link via external_ref).

## Scope (what fz can certify soundly — T6 mechanical facts only)
1. read/ReadSpan: span payload + span_digest + object_digest (needs zero-ref v2 SpanRef).
2. search/ExactSearch: completeness witness = exact-search completeness over a locked byte domain (the searched object set, pinned by digests + fs snapshot identity). The witness must enumerate the searched-domain identity, not just the hits — "0 hits" is only certifiable if the domain is complete (the current fs search literal-only caveat is exactly the failure mode this kills).
3. Diff: old/new ObjectId pair with byte-exact diff payload.
4. mutation receipts: BuildReceipt-style provenance for TransactionJournal outcomes.

## Contract requirements
- Certificates travel inline in the compound-op response envelope (no extra round trip; epic perf law).
- Certificate construction at write/read time in the same pass as CAS hashing.
- Uncertifiable responses are still legal — they simply carry no certificate and must route Expand/RawFallback at the gate; fz must never fabricate a witness.

## done_when
- [ ] Envelope schema agreed and documented hub-side (coordinate with zerostack-surface-shape-consistency-u28 so the certificate field lands inside the SAME canonical result-shape convergence, not as a new divergence)
- [ ] Mirror implementation bead filed in FSZero repo and linked via external_ref
- [ ] FSZero passes hub RACC conformance gates RACC-CERT, RACC-GATE-IRREV, RACC-INLINE, RACC-RESIDENCY
- [ ] No latency regression on read/search hot path (fz is ~6ms/read today; certificate work must amortize into existing hashing)

## Anti-goals
No semantic witnesses; no certificate for fuzzy/regex search unless the domain lock is provable; no second fsync or round trip for certificate storage.
notes: SCOPE ADDITION (paper Thm 7.6, exact streaming-query compression): sparse span reads are NOT the only certifiable class. A locked deterministic streaming operator may scan EVERY byte and return only a small exact sufficient statistic (count, digest, line-stat, aggregate) with a completeness receipt proving all locked input objects were processed. fz aggregation ops (match counts, file stats, tree digests) qualify — certify them under the same witness machinery. This means 'all bytes matter' tasks can still compress massively as long as the aggregation runs backend-side under a locked operator.

title: feat(adoption/gz): GraphZero completeness witnesses under locked parser/index version + sound certificate cache
description:
## Goal
GraphZero adopts the RACC layer: completeness witnesses for graph queries under a LOCKED parser+index version, passing hub RACC conformance. Implementation in the GraphZero repo; this bead tracks the hub contract + sequencing (file the mirror bead in GraphZero when unblocked, link via external_ref).

## Scope (mechanically certifiable graph facts)
1. Definition/References: witness = all-references completeness under (parser_version_digest, index_version_digest, object_digest set). This is the paper's locked-operator condition — without the version pins the witness is UNSOUND.
2. AstClosure: graph closure under declared edge relations (RelationMask) and radius; witness enumerates the closure frontier proof.
3. CallPath/DataflowSlice: path existence certificates with node/edge provenance.

## The versioning discipline (highest-risk item, do first)
GraphZero must expose a stable (parser_version, index_version) identity digest that changes whenever parsing or indexing semantics change. Certificate cache invalidation is keyed by (object_digest, index_version) — stale-version acceptance is a soundness bug, so version identity must join the operation ABI digest (coordinate with zero-abi contract_digest machinery).

## Certificate caching (the big win)
Once witnesses are version-keyed, repeat queries on unchanged objects return cached certificates and SKIP index work entirely — provably sound memoization. Blast-radius/impact pre-warming across sessions becomes safe by construction. Emit cache-hit telemetry for the RADC-D bead.

## done_when
- [ ] Version-identity digest exposed and pinned in ABI (hub-side schema agreed)
- [ ] Mirror implementation bead filed in GraphZero repo, linked via external_ref
- [ ] GraphZero passes hub RACC conformance gates RACC-CERT, RACC-INLINE
- [ ] Cache-key soundness test: certificate accepted iff both object_digest set and index_version match; changing either must invalidate

## Anti-goals
No witnesses over unversioned indexes; no cross-version certificate reuse; no semantic relevance claims in witnesses (T6).
notes: SCOPE ADDITION (Thm 7.6): gz aggregate queries (reference counts, closure sizes, blast-radius summaries) are streaming sufficient statistics — certifiable with a completeness receipt even though they consume the whole index. Same witness machinery, huge savings class.

title: feat(adoption/tz): TokenZero ledger cutover + gate-routed compression decisions
description:
## Goal
TokenZero adopts the RACC layer: wire zero-ledger as the canonical accounting core and drive zero-gate for its compression decisions. Implementation in the TokenZero repo; this bead tracks the hub contract + sequencing (file the mirror bead in TokenZero when unblocked, link via external_ref).

## Scope
1. Ledger cutover: tz's existing billed/raw/recovery/visible token accounting re-expressed through zero-ledger charge() with locked tokenizer identity. The per-response accounting block becomes a zero-ledger receipt fragment; the session-cumulative DominanceReceipt is emitted at session end and on demand.
2. Gate integration: tz's visible-compression decisions (passthrough vs compact vs lossy) route through zero-gate. Lossy elision without a certificate must present as Expand/RawFallback-eligible, never as a silent commit — this structurally fixes the zerostack-spz class (lossy footer-only flagging) because an uncertified lossy span cannot claim certified status.
3. Exposure/replay: re-expansion of a ref charges recovery tokens; the T8 replay identity must hold across expand/re-expand cycles (this is the accounting substrate RADC-D falsifier 3 needs).

## done_when
- [ ] Mirror implementation bead filed in TokenZero repo, linked via external_ref
- [ ] TokenZero passes hub RACC conformance gates RACC-RECEIPT, RACC-BUDGET, RACC-INLINE
- [ ] Session DominanceReceipt emitted with exact_phase_valid recomputable by the harness
- [ ] charge() on the shell hot path adds no measurable latency (existing per-call accounting already exists; this is arithmetic relocation, not new work)

## Anti-goals
No percentage marketing derived from receipts without the task-indexed caveat (T5); no float arithmetic; no second tokenizer pass to recount.

title: CRITICAL TOCTOU: CAS publish never takes the GC coordination lock, so GC unlinks live objects
description:
A publisher and the garbage collector can interleave such that GC unlinks an object a publisher just republished or is about to reference. Publish returns Ok(hash), contains(hash) was true, and the object file is then gone. Later reads are NotFound, not Corruption, so this is silent data loss plus a dangling reference from a committed root. Nothing panics and the GC report claims a clean Collect.

Root cause: publish takes no coordination lock in any engine, and the sweepers pre-unlink recheck inspects only gc/** metadata, never the object identity or mtime.

TokenZero/crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs:
  :77-109   publish() - no lock acquired
  :1134     run_gc() acquires GcCoordLock
  :1213     per-hash recheck: load_mark_state again (metadata only)
  :1217     cas.remove_object(hash) -> unlink
  :178-201  remove_object re-stats only "regular file, not symlink"
  :1079-1092 GcCoordLock::acquire, taken by run_gc and the three record publishers, never by publish

Interleaving (GC left, publisher right):
  1 acquire lock
  2 load_mark_state: h absent from roots/pins/leases, uncertain=false
  3 build_dry_run_report reads h mtime -> age >= min_age -> Collect
  4 write report, persist progress
  5                         publish(bytes) for the same h, no lock. dest exists -> verify_existing -> Ok(h). No mtime touch, no pin, no lease.
  6                         caller records h into an in-flight root/manifest; new snapshot not yet published
  7 recheck load_mark_state: still no reference -> passes
  8 remove_object(h) -> unlink
  9                         publisher commits the root referencing h
  11                        later resolve(h) -> NotFound

Variant B: a fresh publish lands a new inode via create_new + rename for a hash already listed Collect, and step 8 deletes it. min_age is defeated twice: the age came from the pre-rename or pre-republish inode, and remove_object never re-stats mtime.

Per-engine:
- TokenZero: vulnerable and is the deleter. Publish lockless, recheck metadata-only, unlink without identity or mtime recheck and without quarantine.
- FSZero: vulnerable, partially mitigated. It holds an exclusive advisory lock for the whole sweep (src/core/cas.rs:249-251) but put/put_prehashed never acquire it (:146-188), so its own window is identical. touch_blob on existing-put and on get (:161,:197) plus a 7-day grace (:53) reduce exposure but do not close it: a blob older than the grace that gains a new reference without any put or get is still deleted, and TokenZero GC ignores mtime once min_age is satisfied.
- GraphZero: cannot cause it, never deletes (crates/graphzero-store/src/store/gc_roots.rs:11-13), but is a victim. SharedCas::put takes no lock, so TokenZero run_gc on a shared root can unlink a GraphZero object.
- No engine mitigates it fully.

Fix, once, in the hub: one advisory lock at <store_root>/gc/coordinator.lock. Publishers take it Shared across hash -> dest check -> rename -> protection record write; the sweeper takes it Exclusive across mark -> report -> recheck -> quarantine/unlink. remove_object and quarantine_object accept a &StoreLock rather than acquiring one, so the sweeper cannot forget it. Single lock means no lock order and no cycle; both acquisitions are deadline-bounded; kernel releases on process death so no stale reclaim is needed.

Regression test must be deterministic via a GcHooks::before_unlink seam plus channels, not timing: block GC between recheck and unlink, then assert a concurrent protected publish blocks (proof the shared lock is excluded), release, and assert get_verified returns the bytes. Pre-fix behavior is the exact inverse.

Implemented as part of zerostack-sce wave 1.
close_reason: Fixed in all three engines. Root cause confirmed against source: publish/put took no coordination lock in any engine, while only the sweeper held one, so a reference established between the sweeper's metadata-only recheck and its unlink was invisible to it. Fix is the single-lock design from the bead: publishers take the coordinator lock SHARED across hash -> dest check -> rename, the sweeper keeps it EXCLUSIVE across mark -> report -> recheck -> unlink. One lock, so no lock order and no cycle; kernel releases on death; verified nothing acquires it while already holding it, so no self-deadlock. TokenZero (commit 3097dac, the deleter): GcCoordLock gained acquire_shared, publish() takes it, and remove_object() now requires a &GcCoordLock so a sweeper cannot forget it; added a before_unlink hook so the regression pins GC at the exact window via channels rather than timing. FSZero (commit 03795cf): put_prehashed holds the existing .gc.lock shared; gc() already used try_lock so it fails closed with cas_gc_busy. GraphZero (commit 126e031): put_with_limit holds <root>/gc/coordinator.lock shared, the same file TokenZero's sweeper takes, so the two engines coordinate on one lock; also tightened cas_writes_nothing_outside_the_object_namespace to assert the blob namespace exactly plus a one-entry allowlist outside it. Every regression was mutation-tested: removing the shared acquisition turns each red with the exact pre-fix symptom. tokenzero-recovery 188+ pass, fszero core::cas 3/3, graphzero shared_cas_contract 13/13; clippy and rustfmt clean on all touched files. Two pre-existing unrelated failures were confirmed independent by stashing and reproducing at HEAD: fszero codemode::host accounting tests, and graphzero amdahl_cold_index_breakdown (a timing-fraction assertion, reproduced 5/5 at baseline).

title: EPIC: Converge shared CAS, GC, and store-root architecture in zero-store
description:
Unify the durability-critical CAS publish/verify/GC state machine and .zerostack store-root resolution in zero-store, then cut TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero over without byte, path, crash-consistency, or migration drift.

The epic owns extraction, engine adoption, namespacing, path safety, corruption prevention, and measured durability-preserving performance. Engine-specific wrappers may keep aliases, but canonical layout and algorithms live once.
acceptance_criteria: All three engines consume zero-store for canonical CAS/GC/root resolution; no private behaviorally-equivalent copies remain; shared-store collisions and literal-tilde paths are impossible; crash/concurrency tests and digest/path equality gates pass; rollout and rollback are documented.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
Wave 1 part B landed, plus the publish side of part A.

Shipped in crates/zero-store:
- store_root.rs: one resolver for all three engines. Canonical rules, reconciling the three that had drifted: project-local .zerostack outranks the env pin; the pin requires shared-store opt-in; an exported-but-empty pin means unset; a pin outside the project is namespaced as <root>/projects/<key>/<engine>; the project key is 16 lowercase hex of sha256 over the absolutized root path with no prefix; the CAS is shared per store root and never project-namespaced. Engines pass only their own opt-in aliases, so precedence and truthiness live in one place. 21 tests, driven from the golden matrix, including the two gates the engines fail today: distinct projects never collide under one pin (TokenZero fails this, zerostack-ljx) and all three engines derive the same project key (FSZero fails this on its sid- prefix).
- gc_lock.rs: the single store coordination lock at <store_root>/gc/coordinator.lock. Publishers shared, sweeper exclusive. One lock means no lock order and no cycle, so deadlock freedom is structural. Acquisition is deadline-bounded so a wedged holder surfaces as a typed WouldBlock rather than a hang, and the kernel releases on process death so no stale reclaim is needed. The path is deliberately identical to TokenZeros existing GcCoordLock, and both fs4 and std map to flock on Unix, so a hub publisher and a not-yet-migrated TokenZero sweeper interoperate during the cutover.
- cas.rs: publish now runs under the shared guard, which is the publish half of the TOCTOU fix (zerostack-rhd). Added PutOutcome with a created flag, put_outcome, put_prehashed that re-derives and compares the digest so a wrong hash writes nothing, touch, list_objects, and remove_object plus quarantine_object which take a &StoreLock instead of acquiring one, so a sweeper cannot forget the guard. Dedup now refreshes mtime, since a dedup is a fresh reference and an age-based policy that never sees it collects a live object. The temp reaper recognizes all three historical engine shapes, closing the mutual blindness in zerostack-oh7. object_path no longer panics on short input.

Verification: zero-store 8 tests to 45. Workspace 60 to 100, all passing. zero-store is clippy-clean and fmt-clean. The publish/GC race has a deterministic regression test that parks a sweeper between its decision and its unlink using channel rendezvous, asserts a publish is excluded, then asserts the republished object is readable. No timing assumptions anywhere.

Empirically resolved an open question from the design analysis: on rustc 1.97.1 the std signatures are File::try_lock() -> Result<(), std::fs::TryLockError> and try_lock_shared() the same, not Result<bool>. Probed rather than assumed, so no new dependency was needed: fs4 is not required.

Remaining for this bead, the larger half of part A: port the zerostack.cas-gc.v1 state machine itself (records, mark, report, resumable sweep, epoch monotonicity, uncertainty policy) from TokenZero shared_cas.rs:296-1471 into a zero-store gc module, which needs serde promoted from dev-dependency to dependency. Until that lands the lock is in place but the sweeper still lives in TokenZero. Then the engine cutovers: TokenZero by PR, FSZero and GraphZero direct.

Also filed from the analysis of the three implementations: zerostack-rhd, pi1, ljx, oh7, 2x7 in the hub, tokenzero-8tdg, 4xvw, mivh, fszero-1woo, 44nj, p0cz, graphzero-m94u, f2jn.
